LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch as these two teams take center stage on "Thursday Night Football" after Week 7 losses IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect In the Week 8 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Green Bay Packers play host to the Carolina Panthers . The Packers enter this game off a disappointing loss to the division rival Detroit Lions , in a game they had multiple chances to win. Green Bay had won three in a row to salvage its season after a blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons the last time the Packers played on Thursday night (Week 3), but they hit a bump in the road last week. Now, they're looking to make it four wins in five games. The Panthers are coming off an embarrassing blowout loss at the hands of the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Carolina was blasted 43-13 last week and was never truly competitive, falling down 17-0 early. However, the Panthers still sit at .500 after climbing that hump with their win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6. Now, they try to get back to their winning ways. Which of these two teams will get back in the win column? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Packers vs. Panthers live Date: Thursday, Oct. 29 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -3/5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Panthers have the ball The Panthers limped to their worst offensive performance of the season last week, managing just 266 yards, 15 first downs and 13 points while turning the ball over four times. They had previously gained at least 340 yards in every game, gained at least 24 first downs in four of five, and scored 25-plus points in four of five. Bryce Young returned to poor form on Sunday, going only 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while also fumbling once. He's now completed south of 52% of his passes in back-to-back games and south of 55% in three of his last four, with the only exception being a game against the decrepit Lions pass defense. Young got off to a hot start to the season , but he's cooled off a bit as of late. The Packers have been a tough matchup for opposing quarterbacks this year. They're eighth in net passing yards per attempt, and they've yet to allow more than 296 net passing yards in any game this season. They've also allowed just nine touchdown passes against nine interceptions. Jonathan Gannon has been good at limiting what opponents can do through the air, for the most part. It is, however, worth noting that the Packers faced Carson Wentz , Geno Smith , Michael Penix Jr. , Jalon Daniels and Tyson Bagent before getting Dak Prescott and Jared Goff over the last two weeks. So they haven't exactly done this against a murderer's row of opponents. Green Bay has gotten pressure at a below-average rate — no surprise with Micah Parsons still sidelined. Instead, the Packers have gotten by against the pass with sticky coverage and timely plays on the ball. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse have been solid on the outside. Javon Bullard has played well in the slot, and the safeties are providing quality help over the top and in the middle of the field. Carolina's passing game is mostly built outside the numbers with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker , though Young has thrown over the middle more this season than in past years. It'll be up to the skyscrapers on the perimeter to win their one-on-one matchups here in order to give Young room to throw, though he should have more time than he did last week thanks to Green Bay's relatively weaker pass rush. In the run game, the Panthers lean on Chuba Hubbard , who is averaging 4.8 yards per carry in a workhorse role in the absence of Jonathon Brooks . Hubbard only got seven carries in the negative game script last week, but you can likely expect the Panthers to try to "Establish The Run" here as a way to get their offense back on track. Green Bay has allowed only 3.9 yards per carry this season, though, so it might be tough, especially with right tackle Taylor Moton now on the sidelines. When the Packers have the ball The Packers welcomed Josh Jacobs back to the lineup last week but still found themselves entirely unable to run the ball against the Lions. They totaled just 60 yards on the ground, with Jacobs himself carrying 11 times for only 36 yards. Green Bay is now averaging a pathetic 2.9 yards per carry on the season, which unsurprisingly ranks dead last in the league. The Panthers, meanwhile, were run over by the Bucs last week. Bucky Irving and Co. blew past Carolina for a remarkable 258 yards on the ground, which was made all the more incredible by the fact that the Panthers had yielded just 81 rushing yards in their previous two games combined. Still, Carolina has allowed 5.2 yards per carry on the season now, which, to no surprise, ranks dead last. Almost 60% of the rushing yards the Panthers have allowed, though, came in their games against the Bucs and the Chicago Bears in Week 1. They've been fine-ish against the run otherwise. So, can the Packers run the ball with any degree of success here? If the recent history of this season is any indication, then the answer is probably not. Jacobs has been at or below 4.0 yards per carry in two of his last three full seasons, and spending six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list in the wake of a disturbing domestic violence incident probably didn't make him a more efficient runner. And the offensive line is still not a good run-blocking unit. So, the fate of the Packers' offense likely once again falls on the right shoulder of Jordan Love . Love has only completed 59.8% of his passes at an average of 7.4 yards per attempt this season, but he's been victimized by a league-high 21 drops, according to Tru Media. Love is attacking deep downfield consistently, with a 9.1-yard average depth of throw that ranks fourth-highest in the NFL . As such, he's created explosive plays (16-plus-yard gains) at the third-highest rate in the league among 33 qualified quarterbacks. He should see favorable matchups when he looks downfield on Thursday night. Panthers starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain out on injured reserve, which has left rookie Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans as the starting corners. But Evans is also out on Thursday night, meaning, well, I honestly don't even know who is going to step up in his absence. The Panthers elevated Marco Wilson from the practice squad, and they may need to shift Chau Smith-Wade outside. Either way, it's not a great situation for Carolina. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , who is trending to play, should be able to find space down the field against these corners, and then it's just a matter of actually hanging onto the ball when Love puts it on them. Green Bay could have a big night through the air if the Packers can protect Love, which will be made easier by the absence of Panthers edge rusher Jaelan Phillips , who is also out for this game. It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Watson and Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better as of late after a rough start to the season. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. Despite a three-game winning streak earlier this season and a 4-3 record overall, the Packers are in last place in the NFC North heading into Week 8. Bryce Young and the Panthers are in a different spot, as they’re in first place in the weak NFC South despite going 3-3 through their first six games. Carolina lost at home to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 7, and it only has a half-game lead over the Atlanta Falcons in the division. The Panthers won the NFC South last season, but a litany of injuries to open the 2026 campaign have put them in a tough spot to repeat. away.headline: Injuries beginning to take their toll on the Panthers' secondary, offensive line
away.source: The Associated Press- Sports on MSN
away.blurb: “Just wanna see the guys connected,” Panthers coach Dave Canales said. "I just wanna see them excited about going out there and executing the plan. And playing fast, playing the physical brand. And the effort’s been there. Those things are right. But I know that we can make strides with being able to get everybody on the same page, tying in the whole unit.” Moton, the team's longtime right tackle, was able to return to action three weeks ago, but since injured his fibula and has been placed on injured reserve. Ekwonu is expected back in the next month or so. CHARLOTTE, N.C. (AP) — The Carolina Panthers are probably wishing they could petition the NFL for another bye week. Mounting injuries to the secondary and offensive line have begun to take their toll on the Panthers (3-4), who have dropped two straight games and fallen into a tie with the Atlanta Falcons for first place in the NFC South. On Friday, the Panthers fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero after the team allowed Jordan Love to throw for 288 yards and three touchdowns in a 27-19 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Carolina entered the game last in the league in run defense. The Panthers promoted defensive line coach Todd Wash as interim defensive coordinator. Evero's fate may have been sealed when starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson went down in a Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns and were placed on injured reserve. Since then, the two cornerbacks who were replaced Horn and Jackson have suffered injuries. Akayleb Evans was placed on IR last week and Will Lee injured his hamstring against the Packers in the first half and had to leave the game. Canales said the injuries were taken into account when he fired Evero, but added that the decision was based on the big picture and “a lot of information." Things are just as shaky on the offensive line where the Panthers are playing without three starters, including tackles Taylor Moton and Ickey Ekwonu and guard Damien Lewis. Bryce Young was under constant pressure against the Packers. He was hurried 22 times, hit nine times and sacked six times. “We’ve got to make sure we do a good job of giving him solutions when they do have overloaded pressures and zero looks and things," Canales said. "But it wasn’t just that. They got after us with some four-man rushes and some stunts that we didn’t pass off well. That created a little bit of pressure there as well.” Rookie first-round pick Monroe Freeling has struggled at right tackle this season. Running back Chuba Hubbard continues to be a bright spot for the Panthers despite playing behind an offensive line that has struggled to open holes. Hubbard was used extensively against the Packers and gained 81 yards on 22 carries while hauling in a team-high seven passes for 38 yards. He's clearly the only back offensive coordinator Brad Idzik trusts at this point in the season. away.blurb: The Green Bay Packers were defeated by the Detroit Lions by the score of 20-17 on Sunday afternoon. As it stands, though, they fell to 4-3 with the loss. Early in the game against Detroit, the Packers lost starting center Sean Rhyan to an ankle injury, and his backup, Jacob Monk, to a quad injury. away.blurb: After missing three games due to a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand, quarterback Baker Mayfield is back in the lineup for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday as they take on the Carolina Panthers in a critical intra-division game. Mayfield carried a questionable designation on the injury report into the weekend but was able to practice without limitations throughout the week. He intends to wear a specialized glove on his right hand that offers added support to the injured joint, preventing the thumb from being bent backward. Mayfield will not have the team's top receiving target at his disposal, however, as wide receiver Emeka Egbuka is out for Week Seven with both a concussion and a foot injury. In addition, starting right tackle Luke Goedeke is out due to a calf ailment and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. will miss his third straight outing thanks to a rib fracture. The Buccaneers and Panthers submitted their list of inactives at 11:32 a.m. ET on Sunday, 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff of their Week Seven meeting at Bank of America Stadium. After elevating linebacker Caden Fordham from the practice squad, the Buccaneers had 54 available players and thus had to name six inactives to get down to the game-day limit of 48. The Panthers also elevated outside linebacker Nick Hampton and cornerback Robert Rochell from the practice squad and had to name seven inactive players. Carolina will be without one of its top pass-rushers as Jaelan Phillips is out due to a hamstring strain. Fellow outside linebacker Thomas Incoom is also unavailable due to a calf issue, and he was placed on injured reserve on Saturday. home.headline: Packers get exciting injury update on Micah Parsons: Report
home.blurb: The Green Bay Packers expect superstar pass rusher Micah Parsons to return to practice next week, according to a report from NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport on Thursday. “Micah Parsons is expected to return to practice next week. Obviously short week, was not able to do it this week. Next week he should be on the practice field if all goes well. And that is an excellent thing for the Green Bay Packers,” Rapoport said. “I expect caution as far as when he’s actually on the playing field. They want to make sure everything around his knee is as strong as possible. “They are taking their time, but his return is coming.” The Packers will take the field for a “Thursday Night Football” matchup against the Carolina Panthers later this evening. Parsons’ next opportunity to return to the field for in-game action is a Week 9 matchup against the New England Patriots next Sunday. The Packers have been without their generational pass rusher for the entirety of the season thus far, as he continues to recover from the ACL tear he suffered in Week 15 of Green Bay’s 2025 campaign. Green Bay faces off against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 10 before taking their bye in Week 11. Thursday night’s matchup against the Panthers will kick off at 8:15 p.m. ET. home.headline: NFL rumors: Packers star Micah Parsons gets potential return date
home.blurb: “Packers star Micah Parsons is expected to return to practice next week and make his 2026 debut in November, with the most likely return date coming Thanksgiving Eve against the Rams,” NFL insider Tom Pelissero posted on X, formerly Twitter. The Green Bay Packers ’ wait to have Micah Parsons back on the field is almost over. The star pass rusher, who has been rehabbing his injured knee, is nearing his much-awaited season debut, with one game in particular looking likely . Parsons was traded in August 2025 to the Packers by the Dallas Cowboys, then agreed to a record four-year, $188 million contract. He was having a fantastic debut season for Green Bay, recording 12.5 sacks in 14 games. However, he suffered a torn ACL against the Denver Broncos in December and missed their playoff loss to the Chicago Bears. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Despite missing Parsons, the Packers have had no problems getting to the opposing quarterback this season. They currently lead the league with 22 sacks , including six on Bryce Young in their 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers on Thursday night. But of course, it will still be a huge boost for the Packers to add one of the most dangerous pass rushers in the entire league in Parsons to a defense that has already been making a ton of plays under new defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon. Aside from leading the league in sacks, they also have a league-leading 10 interceptions. But before potentially getting Parsons back in Thanksgiving Eve against the Rams, the 5-3 Packers have two more tough games to go. They will go to Foxboro to take on the New England Patriots. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. They need the defense to hold the opponent down entirely, and I'm not sure that even Flores' bunch can do that in the friendly confines of Ford Field. … Prediction: Lions 23, Vikings 14 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) Dajani (Steelers -3.5): How can the Browns keep getting away with this? They overcame a 14-0 deficit in Nashville on Sunday, as Harold Fannin Jr . took a short reception 36 yards down the field with 20 seconds remaining to set up a 32-yard game-winning field goal from Andre Szmyt . Deshaun Watson became the third quarterback since 1970 to register a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of the season. With this being a divisional game against an opponent that just got back from Paris, I can understand why some would take the points with the underdog given the hook. But the Steelers are 3-0 ATS at home. That includes Week 3, when they dropped 30 points on Joe Burrow and the Bengals in a win, and Week 5, when Pittsburgh scored 34 points in a double-digit victory over the Colts. The Steelers are averaging 26.0 points per game over their last five contests, which ranks top 10 in the NFL, and are 8-0 SU and ATS in their last eight home games vs. the Browns. In fact, Pittsburgh is actually a perfect 11-0 ATS in its last 11 home divisional games. Insane stat. … Prediction: Steelers 26, Browns 21 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): I don't understand how the Browns keep doing it. Every single one of their victories has required a game-winning drive in the final five minutes of the game. That's not sustainable on any level whatsoever. The Steelers don't exactly have consistency written all over them, considering the vagaries of their passing game and the fact that their three-game winning streak has come against weak opponents. However, I trust Jaylen Warren and Co. more than I do the Browns at this point. … Prediction: Steelers 20, Browns 13 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) Dajani (Falcons +2.5): I have plenty of questions about both of these teams, but I did tell you the Falcons were going to cover the small number vs. the 49ers last week! Atlanta finished that game on a 26-6 run after trailing 14-3. They scored on four straight drives. I'm not sure the Buccaneers deserve to be three-point favorites this week after that destruction of the Panthers. Baker Mayfield had to throw for just 64 yards and a touchdown in a 43-13 victory, as Bucky Irving , Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker combined for 246 yards rushing and three touchdowns. This Falcons rush defense ranks fourth in the NFL with 88.9 rushing yards allowed per game. Plus, the Falcons have won two road games this season by 20+ points after being listed as an underdog, and are 4-0 ATS in their last four road games against the Buccaneers. … Prediction: Falcons 26, Buccaneers 24 Dubin (Falcons +2.5): The Buccaneers ran all over the Panthers last week, but Atlanta has actually been quite good against the run, allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season. Can Tampa really control the game with Bucky Irving the way it did last week, or will it have to actually turn Baker Mayfield loose as a passer here? If the Bucs have to do that, I have more confidence in Atlanta's offense right now, with Bijan Robinson , Drake London and even Kyle Pitts contributing at a high level. … Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 17 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Dajani ( Broncos +1.5): The Broncos had an embarrassing outing last time they played the Chiefs, allowing 247 yards off of 28 missed tackles in a 31-10 loss. There has been a lot of talk about Bo Nix and the offense, but what about the Chiefs? They averaged 4.3 yards per play and recorded just 213 yards of total offense in that embarrassing loss to the Seahawks. The team seemingly never got off the bus. Both of these teams are considered Super Bowl contenders in the latest odds at the best betting sites , and they feature two of the best quarterbacks in the league. Lamar Jackson (ankle) has not played since the first half of Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans, but he is expected to return on Sunday in what has suddenly become a huge game for the Ravens. Baltimore is 4-3 this season after going 1-2 in the games Jackson missed, and it’s in last place in the AFC North with every team in the division over .500. The Ravens dropped back-to-back key division games against Cleveland and Cincinnati without the two-time league MVP. Josh Allen – the MVP favorite this season – and the Bills are coming out of their bye week to play in this game, and they’re favored at home after a 5-1 start. Buffalo is looking to get the top spot in the AFC, and it benefitted from a Kansas City Chiefs loss (now 5-1 as well) during Week 7. Sunday’s game is the eighth meeting between Jackson and Allen all-time, with the Ravens holding a 3-2 edge in the regular season while Allen has won both of his playoff matchups against Jackson. Who has the edge in this regular-season clash? All season long, the SI Betting team has been predicting the final score of NFL games, and this one is no different. Unfortunately, I place my bets early in the week, so I don't have the benefit of knowing whether or not the two-time MVP will be on the field on Sunday. The betting line indicates that he will, so I'm going to trust that, along with the reports that Jesse Minter is optimistic that Jackson will be ready to go. When a team only has one loss on their schedule, and they have the best quarterback in football on their roster, a lot of their issues are overlooked. That's the case for the Bills, whose defense has been horrendous this season, ranking 30th in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. They are the only defense in football that ranks in the bottom three in both of those metrics. I hesitate to lay more than a field goal on any team with that bad of a defense, especially when that defense potentially has to face another MVP candidate at quarterback. Buffalo’s defense is last in the NFL in EPA/Play and 30th in success rate, so this could be a get-right game for Jackson and Co. if he’s able to play at his full capabilities. Lamar Jackson is back for Baltimore, giving football fans just the treat we wanted: a showdown with Buffalo QB Josh Allen. My Ravens vs. Bills predictions lean into that QB competition and what could be the most fun game on Sunday's slate. Here are my best NFL picks for this AFC heavyweight bout on Nov. 1. TOP Pick Ravens vs Bills prediction: Bills moneyline The return of Lamar Jackson has understandably dragged down the market on the Buffalo Bills . That offers a better ask on the home team's moneyline. The former MVP comes back from an ankle injury just in time, as this offense was getting stale under backup QB Tyler Huntley . But Jackson isn't 100% and his mobility will be tested early by the Bills defense, with the 11th-highest pressure rate per dropback. Baltimore's offensive line might not be up to the challenge, with injuries stacking up. Making plays with his legs has been a huge part of Lamar's success in recent meetings with Buffalo, rushing for 54, 70, and 73 yards in their three most recent matchups. Buffalo has had two weeks to rest and prep for Jackson and the Ravens , coming off a Week 7 bye. That also allows the Bills to get difference makers back on both sides of the ball, including WR1 D.J. Moore and DE Ed Oliver . Not only is Buffalo holding the rest edge, but this is its first home game in new Highmark Stadium in nearly a month. The last time the Bills were in front of the Mafia faithful, they were upset by the rival Patriots in Week 4. A win over Baltimore puts Buffalo back in the driver's seat of the AFC. Allen's nose for the end zone is incredible, and he's scored four total touchdowns in his last two meetings with the Ravens. Allen already has eight rushing touchdowns in six games this year and rumbled for 14 last year, including two touchdowns against the Ravens in their Week 1 shootout. He also scored a pair of tuddies on the ground when Buffalo battled Baltimore in the Divisional Round two seasons ago. away.headline: Ravens injury report: Vega Ioane returns, Lamar Jackson full again
away.blurb: Zenitz also reported on Thursday morning that Lamar Jackson is "on track" to return from his three-game absence. The 29-year-old quarterback was a full participant for a second day in a row; a repeat on Friday would set him up to play against the Bills, but the quick turnaround before Week 8 could be a factor as it was last year. RB Adam Randall (neck, designated to return from IR) CB T.J. Tampa (knee, designated to return from IR) * The rest of the squad is in relatively good shape heading into Sunday. Hawkins will likely miss a second game in a row, but Simpson has been playing with limited practice participation for weeks. The Ravens could slowplay the returns of Tampa and Randall from injured reserve, but both could fortify key areas of the team. The former still has another week to practice before he must be activated, while the latter was only designated to return this week. Comparatively, the Bills had a worse Thursday, downgrading three players. Linebacker Joe Andreessen (knee, limited) and running back Ray Davis (illness, DNP) were both added to the Week 8 injury report, while cornerback Dee Alford (knee) went from limited to DNP. Right tackle Spencer Brown (back) was sidelined for a second day in a row, putting him at real risk of missing Sunday's game. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins was the only player on the active roster to miss practice entirely. Ioane is expected to miss time due to an MCL sprain, but the first-round pick is pushing to play through the injury and take the field against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, per CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz . Even while injured, there is a steep drop-off in play to backups Andrew Vorhees and Emery Jones, and line play has been the offense's kryponite this year. However, this may be a case when the Ravens have to protect a young player from himself, as they have in the past with Hamilton. home.blurb: The Bills come out of their Week 7 bye hoping to get wide receiver D.J. Moore and defensive tackle Ed Oliver back after both missed the previous two games. He did not practice Wednesday or Thursday before the Raiders game but returned on a limited basis Friday and was listed as questionable. Buffalo ultimately kept him inactive. He missed five consecutive practices before returning on a limited basis the Friday before the Raiders game. Oliver was listed as questionable but inactive in Las Vegas. Dalton Kincaid left Buffalo's victory over Las Vegas because of a rib injury but was able to return. The Bills listed him as questionable to return. Kincaid came back in the fourth quarter and caught a 14-yard pass three plays later. Chubb went out during the second quarter and was initially listed as questionable. He returned later in the first half and played 21 of Buffalo's 66 defensive snaps against Las Vegas. T.J. Sanders played against Las Vegas and recorded one tackle after being listed as questionable because of a shoulder injury. His suspension begins Oct. 26 and he can return to Buffalo's active roster Nov. 2, meaning he will miss Sunday's game against Baltimore. Zane Durant is eligible to return after beginning the season on injured reserve. Buffalo can designate Durant to return and open his 21-day practice window when he is medically cleared. Tyrell Shavers is eligible to return after beginning the season on the physically unable to perform list. The Bills can designate him to return and open his 21-day practice window when he is ready. He returned to practice last week and was limited Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. Jackson told reporters Friday that the ankle was improving but that running remained the issue. Baltimore listed Jackson as questionable against the Cincinnati Bengals before ruling him out Saturday. Tyler Huntley started for the third consecutive game and threw for 215 yards in the first half of Sunday's loss. Rookie first-round pick Vega Ioane left the Bengals game near the end of the first quarter because of a knee injury and did not return. home.headline: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) will return Sunday vs. Bills after three-game absence
home.blurb: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) will return Sunday vs. Bills after three-game absence | Latest NFL News, Analysis & Updates | NFL.com Skip to main content GET MORE FOOTBALL WITH NFL+ PREMIUM SUN 6:00PM 6:00PM Chevron Left SUN 6:00PM 6:00PM Jackson was a full participant in practice all week after limited or no participation the last three weeks. He told reporters last Friday that he was dealing with a high ankle sprain but "headed in the right direction," and that his availability would be based on his pain tolerance. Jackson, originally listed as questionable, didn't end up playing in Week 7, but he's good to go for Week 8. Jackson's return is right on time as he and Baltimore are set to face their nemeses in Josh Allen and the Bills. The former is just 2-4 against the latter, including playoffs, in what has become one of this generation's defining quarterback rivalries. Jackson's 2-4 mark is tied for his second-worst among any opponent, per NFL Research. Buffalo came back to beat Baltimore, 41-40, in their most recent meeting, a season-opening matchup last season. This Sunday, Jackson and Co. will return to Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, New York (albeit the newer one), trying to get their season back on track. picks.headline: Why the Titans Will Beat the Bengals in Week 8, Why They Won’t, and a Prediction
picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Bengals in Week 8, Why They Won’t, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Heading into Week, the 1-6 Tennessee Titans have everything to prove, but also nothing at all. Especially after last week’s blown two-score lead to the Cleveland Browns, nobody is expecting Robert Saleh’s first team in Nashville to execute a miraculous turnaround. Draft discussions are already becoming relevant, if that tells you anything. Still, the Titans hit the road to face the Cincinnati Bengals this coming Sunday, and it’s a chance for Tennessee to win their second game in three weeks. That’s somehow still an exciting prospect. To preview the matchup, I’ve got one reason the Titans will beat the Bengals, one reason they won’t, and my own prediction for what will actually happen. Let’s start with the former. Will: Titans’ secondary sees massive uptick Two weeks in a row now, Tennessee has forced at least one interception. The Titans have come down with three picks over the last two games, two of which belong to rising offseason pickup Cor’Dale Flott. Tennessee Titans cornerback Cor'dale Flott (18) intercepts Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) on Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. Tennessee is facing one of the best pass-first teams in the NFL. If Saleh's secondary can find consistency beyond the occasional turnover, the Titans would have more than a fair chance to shut down RB Chase Brown on the ground, too. It's much easier to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins in concept than it is on the field, but doing so is the Titans' key to winning this one. Won’t: Titans can't overcome inconsistent Bengals defense The inverse, of course, is if the Titans' offense continues to suffer. The Bengals have proved themselves beatable against "bad" teams - just see their narrow, one-score win over the 1-6 Miami Dolphins two weeks ago. But Cincinnati also just dismantled the Baltimore Ravens last week, 35-13. The through line is that Cincy scored 30+ points in both of those contests; it comes down to the opposing offense's ability to hang in there when Burrow and his crew get hot. Tennessee ranks 31st in both touchdowns and points per game. Almost everywhere the Bengals are in the top 10 through the air, the Titans are in the bottom 10. Cincy has allowed 20+ points in four of their six games this season. If Cam Ward can get back on his feet in any sense of the saying, another 24-point performance like Tennessee had last week could be enough to at least make this one interesting. However, the Titans may need a little more juice than they've seen yet this season from their QB to stay in it. Prediction: Titans lose, 31-20 Ultimately, I have the Titans falling to 1-7 in this one. We've seen a number of trends solidify that this roster has failed to prove their ability to rise beyond. Carnell Tate is the primary receiver in an otherwise underwhelming offense. The defense can force early turnovers, but can't get late stops when it matters - especially when it comes to tackling. Ward has a better second half than his typically abysmal first, but by the time Tennessee tries to get aggressive, it's too late to make a difference. I expect most of, if not all of these notes to be hit in Week 8. I don't think the Titans will lose in a blowout, but on the road against one of the best offenses in the league, this one already looks like too much for Saleh's team. Last week, the staff went 1/4 due to Tennessee losing to the Browns. Isaiah was the only one to forecast a Titans loss. This week, the rest of us are following his lead. With multiple key players confirmed to sit for the Titans and big roster questions still looming, here's our slate of predictions for Tennessee vs. Cincinnati in Week 8. Lane: Bengals 30, Titans 17 I'm both highly optimistic about the future of this Titans team and terribly pessimistic about their current state. You don't trade Jeffery Simmons and get away with it now and later. I think Tennessee pays for his loss in Week 8. The Cincinnati Bengals have scored 30+ points in two straight weeks, and against a freshly weakened Tennessee defense, I expect that trend to continue. Cam Ward is likely to struggle without Carnell Tate, but the Titans' offense should be able to find relative momentum between the red-hot Tony Pollard and reliable second-year WR Elic Ayomanor I just can't imagine this one going the Titans' way, even then. I was already wary of the Tennessee Titans' motivations heading into their Week 8 road date with the Cincinnati Bengals. Then Tennessee traded All-Pro DT Jeffery Simmons to Chicago Thursday afternoon. That move tacked on an extra point to this surging spread, with Cincinnati now laying -11.5 on Sunday afternoon. My Titans vs. Bengals predictions size up that mountain of chalk as well as the crater Simmons leaves in this Tennessee stop unit. Here are my best NFL picks for Nov. 1. TOP Pick Titans vs Bengals prediction: Over 46.5 One of my first plays of Week 8 was taking the Over in this game. And with Jeffery Simmons swapping out his trademark red sleeves for Chicago orange, I like the Over even more considering the Cincinnati Bengals will do the heavy lifting. Simmons was the shining star and identity of the Tennessee Titans defense. His absence up front will drop the Titans even further down the defensive pecking order, which says something when they're already dead last in DVOA at FTN . The Bengals picked apart a very good Baltimore stop unit in the second half of Sunday's win. They finished with 7.0 yards per play and were a perfect 5 for 5 in the red zone, with Joe Burrow and his talented receiving corps finding their stride. Tennessee's secondary allows the second-highest completion rate and has been burned by multiple big plays, bleeding the fourth most passes of 20+ yards entering Week 8. While the Titans haven't given up many passing touchdowns, they haven't played many QBs on Burrow's level. Titans vs Bengals combo The Bengals do the lion's share of the scoring but don't discount the Titans. Tennessee is playing with pace and faces a Cincy defense that still has work to do. Chase Brown finds the end zone to the cheers of fantasy owners everywhere. He faces a watered-down Titans defense that's allowed six scores to running backs. Tee Higgins' projections call for as many as 91 yards against a Tennessee secondary giving up explosive plays. Chase Brown touchdown Tee Higgins 70+ receiving yards Titans vs Bengals touchdown scorer: Chase Brown If anyone was happy to see Simmons traded before Week 8, it was Bengals running back Chase Brown. He no longer has to worry about one of the premier run stoppers in the game, facing a Tennessee red-zone defense now missing its biggest cog. Even when Simmons was in the mix, Tennessee had allowed six scores to rival RBs. Brown has only one touchdown in 2026 despite 13 carries and three receptions in the red zone. Due to that drought, we're getting a discount on his ATTD market in Week 8 considering this prop was trading around 60% two games ago. Given the massive spread, Cincinnati will be in a run-positive game script in the second half of Sunday, helping boost Brown's TD probabilities. His TD forecasts range between 60% and 78%, given he's a threat to run one in or catch a touchdown pass. Titans vs Bengals player prop: Tee Higgins 70+ receiving yards Cincinnati has arguably the best one-two punch at receiver in the NFL, with Tee Higgins serving as "Robin" to Ja'Marr Chase's "Batman". But don't tell Higgins that. He looked more like Superman in Week 7, putting in a monster effort in the win over the rival Ravens. He caught six of seven balls his way for 148 yards and a touchdown. That includes a 44-yard dinger on a broken play with Burrow dodging pressure. We mentioned the Titans' problems giving up home runs over the top, and Higgins is one of the best deep threats in the land, averaging 21.6 air yards per reception and amassing eight catches for 20+ yards. Tennessee has also been burned by WR2s to start the season, rating 24th in DVOA vs. WR2s at FTN while giving up almost 56 yards per game to those second options. Higgins' Week 8 models are very bullish on his receiving yards, ranging from 65 to a high of 91. Most forecasts come in above 80 yards, and my projection sits just shy of 81 yards receiving. This time, though, the Bengals will have more success pushing the ball downfield early and will build a two-score lead in the first half. The Tennessee Titans have kept games close, but they've largely faced weaker competition. Expect the Bengals to step on the gas and cover the 10.5-point spread. Cam Ward throws two interceptions Ward has thrown an interception in five straight games heading into Sunday, and Cincinnati's will be one of the best defensive backfields he has faced this season. DJ Turner is playing like an elite cornerback who is about to get paid a lot of money, and Dax Hill is living up to his billing as the complement to Turner that makes the duo so dangerous. Ward will try to force a ball to Carnell Tate, but Turner will intercept it. Then Cincinnati's defensive line will get pressure on Ward, forcing him to rush a throw that Barrett Carter will pick off.

home.blurb: Bengals officially declare one player out, another questionable for Week 8 matchup against Titans Skip to content The Cincinnati Bengals released their third and final injury report ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Cincinnati has officially declared one player out, and another questionable for Sunday's game against Tennessee. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) is officially out, and linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) is officially questionable against the Titans. Coach Zac Taylor said at the beginning of the week Dugger would not play and is “week-to-week” after aggravating his calf injury last week against the Baltimore Ravens. Giles-Harris figures to be a game-time decision, and his status may be foreshadowed depending on whether or not the club elevates LB Emany Johnson off the practice squad Saturday. As expected, Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) is good to play despite missing Wednesday. Defensive tackles Jonathan Allen, B.J. Hill, and Dexter Lawrence II all had standard rest days. Running back Tyjae Spears (knee), wide receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder), and punter Tommy Townsend (left knee) have all been declared out. None of them practiced at all this week, including Tate, the former Ohio State Buckeye and No. 4 overall pick from the 2026 NFL Draft. WR Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable. Assuming he plays, it'll be him, Elic Ayomanor, and Wan'Dale Robinson leading quarterback Cam Ward's passing attack with Tate sidelined. Starting tight end Gunnar Helm may also see a rise in involvement. He caught four passes for 24 yards last week against the Cleveland Browns. DT John Franklin-Myers (groin) is also questionable, along with cornerback Jaylon Jones (knee), and LB Dorian Mausi (foot). Mausi is still on the Reserve/Injured list and is ineligible to play unless Tennessee activates him to its 53-man roster. Against Philadelphia, the Cowboys finished 9-for-14 on third/fourth downs and reclaimed their spot among the Top 5 attacks in Week 7. The Arizona Cardinals defense has been at the mercy of a very tough schedule, and it shows in its ratings (28th in EPA/play). While the offense was able to counter their opponents' scores earlier in the year, Arizona's attack is sputtering with the third-lowest points per play average over the last three contests. Dallas is more than happy turning this game into a track meet and thrives on the clean indoor surface at AT&T Stadium. Dak Prescott especially enjoys Jerry's World, with his career metrics spiking at home (103.4 rating at home vs. 92.8 on road). This is Dallas first "normal" home game since Week 2 (played TNF at home in Week 5), and I'm grabbing this Cowboys offense short of the key number of a touchdown. Cardinals vs Cowboys combo Arizona was in a similar shootout spot with Detroit a few weeks back and couldn't keep pace with an explosive offense. Dallas does the same here, pulling away with plenty of points in the second half. CeeDee Lamb is coming off a two-TD day in Week 7 and faces a Cardinals defense allowing the second most touchdowns to rival receivers. Michael Wilson needs to be more involved, and Mike LaFleur knows it. With Arizona playing from behind, plenty of passes come his way, and projections call for as many as 70 yards on Sunday. Lamb will rip through an Arizona secondary ranked among the worst in the land but also featuring plenty of bodies on the injury report in Week 8. The Cardinals run one of the highest rates of zone coverage, and Lamb is excellent at spotting seams in that defense. He's not only a downfield threat but also a catch-and-run weapon, exploiting an Arizona stop unit giving up the seventh most yards after the catch. The Cardinals have allowed 10 touchdowns to WRs (second most), and Lamb's TD forecasts for Week 8 all sit at 60% or higher, with some projections at 80%. away.headline: Cowboys defenders Quinnen Williams, Caleb Downs added to injury report vs. Cardinals
away.blurb: Rookie defensive back Caleb Downs was limited in a walkthrough practice with an ankle injury. Defensive tackle Quinnen Williams was also a new addition to the injury report as he's dealing with a hamstring injury. He was limited on Wednesday. FRISCO - The Cowboys added some new names to the injury report Wednesday. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Tuesday that there were a few players dealing with some minor injuries, but nothing significant. The Cowboys could also be on the verge of some players returning . Safety PJ Locke III (foot) and outside linebacker Marist Liufau (forearm) were both full participants Wednesday. Locke was added to injured reserve after hurting his foot in the Week 2 win over the Washington Commanders. Liufau fractured his forearm in the preseason finale. The Cowboys created one roster spot earlier this week when they waived running back Emari Demercado. He was claimed by the Houston Texans on Wednesday. If the Cowboys activate both Locke and Liufau, they'll have to make one more roster move. Cowboys safety Jalen Thompson, another player on injured reserve , was seen working in the rehabilitation group during practice. He's been on injured reserve since he suffered a hamstring injury in late September. His practice window hasn't been opened yet. Read this story on dallasnews.com

home.headline: Cowboys defenders Quinnen Williams, Caleb Downs added to injury report vs. Cardinals
home.blurb: Rookie defensive back Caleb Downs was limited in a walkthrough practice with an ankle injury. Defensive tackle Quinnen Williams was also a new addition to the injury report as he's dealing with a hamstring injury. He was limited on Wednesday. FRISCO - The Cowboys added some new names to the injury report Wednesday. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Tuesday that there were a few players dealing with some minor injuries, but nothing significant. The Cowboys could also be on the verge of some players returning . Safety PJ Locke III (foot) and outside linebacker Marist Liufau (forearm) were both full participants Wednesday. Locke was added to injured reserve after hurting his foot in the Week 2 win over the Washington Commanders. Liufau fractured his forearm in the preseason finale. The Cowboys created one roster spot earlier this week when they waived running back Emari Demercado. He was claimed by the Houston Texans on Wednesday. If the Cowboys activate both Locke and Liufau, they'll have to make one more roster move. Cowboys safety Jalen Thompson, another player on injured reserve , was seen working in the rehabilitation group during practice. He's been on injured reserve since he suffered a hamstring injury in late September. His practice window hasn't been opened yet. Read this story on dallasnews.com

home.headline: Cowboys news roundup: Injury report, Jerry changes deadline tune, Demercado new home
home.blurb: This marks the second straight week that Dallas will be without both Turpin and Winters. According to Archer, of the players with questionable designations, Schoonmaker is the most up in the air. That would indicate that the Cowboys will have Pickens and Clark on Sunday against Arizona. Of course, Jeremiyah Love will return to play against Dallas. Stuff like that always seems to happen. Michael Wilson is also playing after an injury scare this week, and Zaven Collins will be battling through illness in Week 8. Bullard returned to practice in the middle of the week after missing the last four games due to a calf injury he sustained in Week 3. It is unknown if he will make his return this week, and the Cowboys don't particularly need more bodies at defensive tackle, but he is officially questionable for Sunday. This is somewhat of a change of tune from Dallas' owner, as just last week , he foresaw himself being active at the deadline. And there are a handful of intriguing trade targets out there, but the Cowboys have already made deals for Joey Porter Jr. and Broderick Jones since the very end of August. The Dallas Cowboys avoided disaster on Monday Night Football in Week 7 with their convincing win over the Philadelphia Eagles. What the team hasn't done, though, is convince the fanbase that they are a legitimate threat to get into the playoffs and make any kind of run. That's still to be determined. But a big step can be taken in that direction if Brian Schottenheimer's squad can handle business against the Arizona Cardinals, whom they have historically struggled against. Stringing together two wins in this easy stretch of the schedule would do wonders for the team and the fanbase's psyche. And with the trade deadline looming after Week 9, tensions are heightened around the league. The butterfly effect of every move will be felt throughout the NFL. There's a lot to keep track of during this time, and there is no shame in missing any news surrounding your favorite team. That's why we're here: to provide you with the latest Cowboys news from this week that didn't make major headlines or flew under the radar. We'll go through the final Week 8 injury report for both teams, analyse Jerry Jones' latest quote about the deadline, talk Emari Demercado's new home, and more. Cowboys' final Week 8 injury report Here is the Cowboys' final injury report before their Week 8 game against the Arizona Cardinals, courtesy of ESPN's Todd Archer. Bullard and Liufau are both returning from IR stints, and neither had been activated to the 53-man roster yet, as of this writing. But it is possible that the former makes his first appearance since Week 3, and the latter has his season debut after getting hurt in the preseason finale. Stephen Jones also said on 105.3 The Fan that Jalen Thompson is "coming along nicely." Downs' injury status was somewhat of a question mark this week, as was Locke's as he returned from injury. home.headline: Eagles Week 7 injury report vs. Cowboys: Are Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith playing?
home.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles have different answers on two offensive stars entering Week 7 against the Dallas Cowboys . DeVonta Smith is out with a hamstring injury, while Saquon Barkley remains questionable despite finishing the practice week as a full participant. Barkley’s Saturday upgrade is encouraging, but it does not confirm he will play. Philadelphia must still prepare for the possibility of being without its featured running back alongside an already unavailable receiving weapon. Barkley progressed from limited participation Thursday and Friday to full participation Saturday while managing his hamstring injury. That is a positive practice trajectory, particularly compared with remaining limited or missing the final session. However, the Eagles retained his questionable designation. The appropriate conclusion is that playing remains possible, not that he has been cleared for an unrestricted role. The loss is significant. Smith has 26 catches for 310 yards and two touchdowns in four appearances this season. He caught seven passes for 75 yards and a touchdown against Carolina in Week 6, making his absence another interruption after a productive return. Philadelphia also ruled out Dontayvion Wicks , who missed all three practices with an ankle injury. Losing both receivers reduces the available options and complicates how the offense distributes opportunities. Grant Calcaterra and Eli Stowers are questionable despite three full practices, reinforcing why participation alone cannot settle availability. Landon Dickerson followed Barkley’s progression, moving from two limited practices to full participation Saturday. He remains questionable with knee and pectoral injuries, adding uncertainty to the blocking picture. Defensively, Michael Carter II and Nolan Smith are out after three missed practices, with abdomen and concussion injuries, respectively. Jonathan Greenard is questionable after missing Friday and Saturday with an ankle injury. Jalyx Hunt remained limited throughout the week and is questionable, as is Jakorian Bennett despite full participation. Smith’s situation is settled after three missed practices. Barkley’s is not, leaving the Eagles to balance optimism about his progress with uncertainty about his availability and potential workload. home.headline: Cowboys-Eagles final injury update has 7 ruled out including Smith
home.blurb: Running back Saquon Barkley is on track to appear for the first time since leaving the Week 4 game early, and should bring a huge boost to a running game that has floundered the last three weeks. Hopefully ready to meet him in the hole is linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who hasn't seen action since Week 1 for the Cowboys. The Cowboys also expect CB Cobie Durant to return to action, and he hasn't played since Week 2. Those are two big additions for Dallas. Things are trending right for several other Cowboys, though they aren't quite ready to return to action. The Cowboys opened the 21-day practice window for LB Marist Liufau and safety PJ Locke. Both were expected to be key reserves this year and still could be activated before Monday's game, with corresponding roster moves. Starting safety Jalen Thompson can have his window opened next week. Meanwhile, Dallas did rule out WR/KR Kavontae Turpin (ribs) and LB Dee Winters (calf), along with OT Drew Shelton. McKee won't have his top two receivers as both DeVonta Smith and Dontarin Wycks have been ruled out. Barkley is one of seven listed as questionable, along with OF Landon Dickerson and edge rusher Jonathan Greenard, who is expected to be a game-time decision . This article originally appeared on Cowboys Wire: Cowboys-Eagles final injury update has 7 ruled out including Smith The Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles likely never saw these circumstances coming. Predicted to battle for the NFC East title, both teams are still in contention, but are hardly the type of outfits that look ready to make any noise come January. Entering their Week 7 Monday Night Football matchup, the teams sport identical 2-4 records after six games , with injuries the underlying factor of both club's malaise. Dallas, implementing a new defense under first-year coordinator Christian Parker, has seen their back-seven progressively decimated week by week, undermining his attempt to get his footing as a scheme designer and playcaller. The Eagles have just lost body after body throughout their roster, losing key contributors to the offense. Are the clubs trending in opposite directions despite losing streaks for both ? Injury wise, Dallas is starting to get some contributors back, with the question being about whether they can actually make a difference or is Parker's scheme a bad one. The Eagles are trending down, still, though they will get a big boost from one returning member. For Philly, the injury discussion has centered around QB Jalen Hurts and the controversy over his blood clot diagnosis . Regardless of the inner workings there, he's been moved to IR and is done for the year, opening the door for Tanner McKee to get the start and raising the possibility if he flounders, the Eagles could turn to Joe Milton III at QB. Philly snatched him off of Dallas' practice squad last week . Here's a look at the complete injury report from Saturday.

I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17 Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. The Vikings, which have yet to lose a game this season (6-0), feature both a bottom-10 offense (20.8 points/game) and the league's top defensive unit. Coordinated by Brian Flores, Minnesota's defense has permitted just 12.3 points a game, and hasn't allowed more than 16 points in a game since Week 2. And most recently, the Vikings surrendered just 10 points in a 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7. Additionally, Minnesota has been extremely stout against the pass thus far this season. In fact, Kevin O'Connell's squad has allowed the second-fewest passing yards (930) and the least amount of touchdowns through the air (three) through the season's first seven weeks. The Vikings have also already secured seven interceptions, spearheaded by cornerback Byron Murphy's league-high three picks. So, Lions signal-caller Jared Goff, who has yet to throw an interception in 2026, will face arguably his biggest test of the campaign against Minnesota's stingy pass defense . Then on the opposite side of the ball, Detroit's secondary will receive one of its toughest assignments of the year, going head-to-head with All-Pro wideout Justin Jefferson. Jefferson, who has surpassed 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first six NFL seasons, has accumulated 302 reception yards and three touchdowns in five games this season. He's unquestionably Vikings passer Kyler Murray's go-to target and one of the very best receivers in the game today. Subsequently, D.J. Reed, the Lions’ No. 1 cornerback , should get the majority of one-on-one reps with the Pro Bowl pass-catcher. Additionally, I wouldn't be surprised if Detroit defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard deployed a rotation of corners in the Week 8 tilt. And as a result, I could see the likes of Ennis Rakestraw and Roger McCreary also getting opportunities to defend Jefferson Sunday. It'll hardly be an easy task for the Lions’ defensive backs group. However, Detroit does have a solid track record against Jefferson, having limited him to under 60 yards the past three meetings between the NFC North rivals . And if the Lions could do it a fourth straight time, it would go a long way toward Dan Campbell's squad notching its fifth victory on the season. At this present juncture, I'm willing to give Detroit a 61 percent chance to secure the Week 8 victory . picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for the Lions-Vikings NFC North Showdown
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for the Lions-Vikings NFC North Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Practice 3 TRENDING College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates Colts open to trading JT Steph breaks Luka's ankles Belichick-Hudson breakup Three Bold Predictions for the Lions-Vikings NFC North Showdown (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Dakota Allen Fri, October 30, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFC North is officially the most explosive division in football, and Ford Field will serve as ground zero this Sunday. The 4-2 Detroit Lions are fresh off a thrilling, last-second 20-17 victory over the Green Bay Packers. They are set to host the league's final remaining undefeated juggernaut: the 6-0 Minnesota Vikings. This Week eight clash is a textbook battle of strengths. Head coach Dan Campbell has Jared Goff playing at an early-season MVP level, engineering an electric offense. Meanwhile, Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores is piloting a historic, blitz-heavy defensive unit that is suffocating opposing quarterbacks. With massive divisional implications on the line, here are three bold predictions for this highly anticipated rivalry game. 1. Jared Goff Extends Interception-Free Streak to 7 Games Despite Massive Blitz Brian Flores' defense leads the NFL in blitz percentage (38%) and thrives on turning ordinary passing downs into an absolute nightmare. The Vikings' defense has already forced 11 takeaways and racked up 21 sacks. Statistically, Flores loves to force opposing quarterbacks into hurried mistakes. The first bold prediction is that Jared Goff will throw for over 275 yards, multiple touchdowns, and maintain a completely clean sheet with zero turnovers. Goff is currently on an unbelievable heater, throwing 14 touchdowns to zero interceptions through six games. While Flores will throw a kitchen sink of disguised coverages and loaded fronts at him, Goff boasts a stellar 127.1 passer rating against the blitz this season. Shielded by one of the best offensive lines in football, Goff will stay calm in the pocket, pick apart the blitz, and keep the football safe. 2. Jahmyr Gibbs Cracks 120+ Rushing Yards The Vikings have given up very little through the air, ranking near the top of the league in passing defense. However, if their elite unit has a minor vulnerability, it is on the ground. Last week, the Indianapolis Colts exposed some cracks by carving up Minnesota for 154 rushing yards. The second bold prediction is that Jahmyr Gibbs will erupt for over 120 rushing yards and a touchdown. Gibbs has been an absolute workhorse for Detroit, averaging an astounding 103.3 rushing yards per game. Though Flores historically found success neutralizing Gibbs last season, Drew Petzing's offensive scheme will counter Minnesota's aggressive defensive stunts by leaning heavily on the ground game. Gibbs will tire out the Vikings' pass-rushers, hit the secondary at full speed, and log his biggest performance of the year. 3. Lions Hand the Vikings Their First Loss of the Season Minnesota's 6-0 start has been heavily reliant on their elite defense. Kyler Murray and the Vikings' offense have regularly stalled, ranking 29th in total yards per game and managing just 20.7 points per game. To make matters more difficult, starting running back Aaron Jones Sr. is severely limited with a knee injury. The final bold prediction is that the Detroit Lions will win a high-scoring thriller, handing Minnesota its first loss of the 2026 season. The returning presence of Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch gives Detroit's secondary the physical playmaking identity needed to keep Justin Jefferson under wraps. Ford Field will be deafening, and Detroit's offensive versatility will simply be too much to contain for all four quarters. Expect the Lions to walk away with a definitive statement win to tighten the race for the NFC North crown.
