away.headline: Vikings may catch a break with Micah Parsons' injury timeline
away.blurb: Parsons suffered a torn ACL last December, and reports emerged Saturday that he’s expected to return to practice next week. He’s reportedly targeting the Thanksgiving Eve game against the Rams to make his season debut, which is one week after Green Bay hosts the Vikings. The Vikings have gotten off to a perfect 6-0 start, but a road test on Nov. 15 against the Packers is approaching on the horizon. It appears likely that Green Bay will be without its superstar pass rusher, Micah Parsons, for that game. Parsons became one of the most feared pass rushers in the NFL with 52.5 sacks across his first four seasons with the Dallas Cowboys. The Packers acquired him before last season via a blockbuster trade, and he carried that production to Green Bay with 12.5 sacks in 14 games before suffering a season-ending injury last year. Green Bay has turned to an assortment of players to replace Parsons’ production, mainly former first-round pick Lukas Van Ness, who leads the team with 4.5 sacks this season. The Vikings had their highest-scoring output of the season when they beat the Packers 39-22 without Parsons in Week 1. Injuries are obviously not linear, so things could change, but it appears that Green Bay will be without its star pass rusher on Nov. 15 against the Vikings. away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his three-week window opened to return from IR this week but will not return this week. Starting slot cornerback Roger McCreary was a late addition to the Lions' injury report on Friday, when he was limited with a foot injury. He is questionable for Sunday's game, which means he's likely to play. For the Vikings, close to a clean sheet with just a late addition of Jay Ward to the injury report on Friday with knee issue. He was limited on Friday and listed as questionable, but again that means he's likely to play. So, looks like full rosters will be available for both teams on Sunday, except for those on IR. picks.headline: Steelers vs. Browns Bold Predictions: Aaron Rodgers Hit New Milestone
picks.blurb: PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers face one of their toughest tests in Week 8, as they take on the Cleveland Browns and attempt to assert themselves as a top team in the AFC North. The Browns are no easy challenge this time around, and the Steelers learned that firsthand several weeks ago. The Browns won their first meeting on Thursday Night Football, but the matchup shifts to Acrisure Stadium for Week 8, and the Steelers intend to exact some revenge on their divisional foes. Both squads enter with a 5-2 record and a share of the AFC North lead. It’s a measuring-stick showdown between the Steelers and Browns, and bold actions will be taken. Both Teams Score 25 Points or More Both of these franchises bring strong defenses to their Week 8 contest. The Steelers rank in the top 10 in total yards allowed per game, rushing yards allowed per game and points allowed per contest. They also rank 11th in passing yards allowed per game. Similarly, the Browns rank in the top 15 across multiple defensive categories. It’s going to be a matchup of two stout defensive units, right? Well what would be more surprising than these two teams putting up an offensive showdown? That’s what could be in store for these two teams, despite all signs pointing toward the opposite. The Steelers rank 22nd in the NFL in points per game, posting an average of 21.9. The Browns trail, recording the 28th-best average of 19.0 points per game. But, the Steelers have also reached the 24-point mark four times in seven tries, and they could put up even more in Week 8. Aaron Rodgers Hits 300 Yards for First Time With Steelers If the Steelers are going to buck the trend and put up points, there are two approaches to help accomplish that. One is to exploit their 19th-ranked run defense, which has to be at the top of their game plan as Jaylen Warren continues to put up MVP-caliber production. Another avenue, the more unexpected one for the offense to take, is to push the ball downfield with the passing game. In the team’s first matchup against the Browns, Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf posted five receptions on nine targets for 115 yards. And they managed to break off his biggest play of the game by getting him away from Cleveland’s top defender, Denzel Ward. If the Steelers can capture that again in Week 8, quarterback Aaron Rodgers could have a magical day. In 2025, Rodgers never hit the 300-yard mark. His 2026 season high so far is 299 yards, which he threw for during that previous contest against the Browns. In the three weeks since, he hasn’t surpassed 255 yards, but this could be the one where he eclipses 300 yards. Germie 100-Yard Game Incoming If Rodgers is throwing that many yards, one of his receivers has to have an outstanding day on the stat sheet. After he earned more and more trust, Bernard could face a favorable matchup if he doesn’t go against Ward too often. He’s gotten close, putting up two 80+ yard games so far this season. This week, it finally happens. The second-round pick eclipses 100 yards for the first time in his young NFL career. Our staff weighs in. Mike Nicastro : The Steelers haven't lost to the Browns twice in a season in almost three decades, but this year presents a unique challenge. Teams traveling internationally over the last two seasons are just 1-7 when returning to face a team that did not travel overseas the prior week. That one win was the Broncos last season, when they scored 33 4th quarter points against the Giants to win by 1 point. Fatigue will play a factor, but having home field will help significantly. This is still a Browns team that lost to the Jets on the road, and just went to the wire with the Titans. Won't be surprised if its ugly, but Pittsburgh rides the run game again into their bye. Steelers 20 Browns 17. Jason Aponte: This will be a dogfight between the division rivals. The Steelers have shown improvement offensively lately and will need to beat Cleveland's plan of man coverage. Rodgers and the offense does enough and the defense holds up to give Pittsburgh the division lead. Steelers 21, Browns 17. Ryan Parish : The Steelers were the better team in 3 out of 4 quarters the last time these teams met a few weeks ago. Both teams have found a groove since, and they enter the contest at 5-2. Winner leaves the game atop the AFC North. I've had a running bit in these predictions that will not change until it stops working. Browns 24-Steelers 23. Austin Bechtold: The Steelers haven't lost to the Browns at home in the regular season since I was two. I can't fathom it happening with how the Steelers defense is playing right now. I've been wrong about Patrick Graham and doubted his scheme to a degree early in the season, but if he calls a great gameplan Sunday I'm sold. Aaron Rodgers is playing his best football since 2021. The Browns aren't the old Browns and I think are better than people are giving credit for. The Steelers do what it takes, and will be in sole possession of first place in the AFC North on Sunday. Steelers 24-18. Ryland Bickley : This is a series that has been defined by home teams winning as of late, and with the Steelers on a hot streak and playing in Acrisure this Sunday, I don't expect that to change. Cleveland's man coverage scheme should once again prove a challenge for the Pittsburgh offense, but the Steelers defense has taken some strides since the last matchup. Steelers 27, Browns 20 . Joey Bray : When these teams take the field on Sunday, the Pittsburgh Steelers will be exactly one month removed from suffering another loss to the Browns in Cleveland on Thursday Night Football. Since that game, the Steelers have won three straight. I can't say for certain how much the team has grown since then, as they still have concerns in the secondary on defense and struggles in the red zone as an offense. Unlike last time where the browns jumped out to a big lead early, I think this game will be a close one throughout. The Browns are a much better football team that anyone anticipated entering the season. Todd Monken deserves a ton of credit for the way he has continued to put Deshaun Watson and the offense in positions to win. However, all five of their wins have come on game winning drives, a trend that is unlikely to continue. I'll take Pittsburgh to get their revenge on Cleveland and go into the bye week with sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Steelers 21, Browns 20 . Jarrett Bailey: I said ahead of the Saints game that I don't know if the Steelers are a team I'd bank on winning four games in a row, yet here we are after a three-game win streak. The whole "Cleveland hasn't won in Pittsburgh since 2003" doesn't necessarily mean much to me in terms of results. Although it does seem to matter when these two teams play in Cleveland that the Steelers turn into the worst versions of themselves. I do think the Steelers win, but I'm not going to take this Browns team lightly. Steelers 20, Browns 16. Let us know what you think in the comments . picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Browns picks: Still Curtain panel predicts grueling AFC North fight - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Practice 3 TRENDING College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates Colts open to trading JT Steph breaks Luka's ankles Belichick-Hudson breakup Cleveland Browns defensive end Adin Huntington, Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Pawloski Sat, October 31, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Almost no predictions believe the biggest AFC North matchup of the season to date will become a blowout victory for either side. The Pittsburgh Steelers will host the shocking 5-2 Cleveland Browns in a venue where the visiting club hasn't won since 2003. Most are picking the Steelers to emerge as the winners of this divisional battle , but don't be shocked if this one comes down to the wire. Both teams go into this matchup not being taken seriously. Perhaps if one of the two dominated this game and pulled away on the scoreboard, then some experts might believe in them. If not, then no matter who wins or loses, this game might fail to gain respect. Either way, the Steelers need to take care of business in their home venue, but this might be their biggest test of the campaign yet. Cleveland hasn't beaten anyone special to this point in the season, but the same can be said for Pittsburgh. It will be interesting to see how the outcome of this game affects whoever eventually wins the AFC North. You would have to assume the victor of this game will be the early favorite to win the division this season. It's not going to be an easy battle to win, and the high stakes only intensify this rivalry. Still Curtain contributors predict a Pittsburgh Steelers season defining victory "The Cleveland Browns have performed better than anyone expected this season but predicting them to sweep the Steelers this season feels rich. The Browns haven't won a regular-season game in Pittsburgh since 2003. Worse yet for Cleveland, they haven't swept the Steelers during the regular season since 1988. Mike McCarthy isn't going to let that happen on his watch." - Tommy Jaggi (Steelers 24-17) "Cleveland is surely talking a big game, and it would be awfully embarrassing to prove their words right. To be frank, neither of these teams is as good as their 5-2 record, but this still feels like it has the makings of a good game. If Pittsburgh loses, it will be a bitter pill to swallow. I think they put the Browns back in their place with a close win." - Andrew Falce (Steelers 24-20) "The Pittsburgh Steelers don't want to squander a chance to give Mike McCarthy his first taste of ranking first in AFC North with a win against the Cleveland Browns. Patrick Graham's defense plays a lot better than in Week 4, forcing DeShaun Watson to make slower, harder decisions as a QB. Aaron Rodgers and Jaylen Warren lead McCarthy's offense to an effective afternoon." - Loyal Ricks Jr. (Steelers 28-20) Final prediction has Steelers finding a way to squeak out a win Score Prediction: Steelers 23, Browns 20 Everyone should predict this AFC North clash to be a close game that comes down to the wire. Expect turnovers to be monumental in the outcome of this game. The Steelers offense needs to play a smart brand of football. Establish the run early and take care of the football. Any opportunities they give the Browns based on Pittsburgh shooting themselves in the foot could be costly. Cleveland has struggled against lesser foes this season but so have the Steelers. That being said, overall, the Black and Gold have the edge when it comes to the talent on their roster. Trusting Aaron Rodgers to win the game over Deshaun Watson provides a clear edge. This won't be an easy game to win, but if the offense can have a strong rushing attack and take care of the football, then they should have a steady path to victory. On the defensive side of things for Pittsburgh, it's all about creating havoc for the opposition. Stop the run first and get Watson on the ground often. Create dysfunction for the quarterback and don't allow him to escape the pocket for big gains. Forcing a couple of turnovers and winning the turnover margin will be vital to getting a win. It's easier said than done, but the Steelers have the players to make this happen. At the end of the day, pick the Steelers to win this AFC North matchup. It's not going to be pretty, as these two teams are eerily similar at this point in the season. Neither has done terrific things thus far, but they have found a way to get to impressive 5-2 records. The Steelers have the talent to win this game, and there should be a strong chance that they do as long as they take care of the ball. away.headline: Browns got a shot in the arm ahead of facing the Steelers thanks to some great injury news
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: The only real question marks for the Browns going into this game are on the injury report. Slot cornerback Myles Harden is listed as questionable with a hamstring injury. On the other side of the ball, right tackle Tytus Howard is questionable after spending the week in concussion protocol. Additionally, depth defensive back and special teamer Daniel Thomas is questionable to play. The Cleveland Browns are getting back a key piece of their defense against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 8. The Cleveland Browns have a chance to move to 6-2 Sunday when they visit the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 8 . It’s an AFC North rematch, and Cleveland needs a road win to sweep the season series after beating Pittsburgh at home on Thursday Night Football back in Week 4. The Browns haven’t swept the Steelers since the 1980s, so pulling it off would be a bit of a shock. Still, Cleveland has put itself in position to do it. The schedule is a bit unusual, with these two teams meeting twice before Week 8 ends. A win would put the Browns firmly in the playoff chase, and they’re getting help on the defensive line at the right time. Browns DT Mike Hall Jr. returns for Week 8 against Pittsburgh The Browns lost defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr. to an ankle injury just before halftime in that Week 4 win over the Steelers. Hall returned in the second half and recorded his only sack of the season in that game. Since then, Hall has missed the last three games for Cleveland. The good news for the Browns is that the third-year defensive tackle will be back on the field Sunday . Hall is the Browns’ third defensive tackle behind Mason Graham and Maliek Collins, and getting him back adds depth to a defense that carries this team. Cleveland also got Graham back last game after he missed a couple of games. With Hall now returning, the defensive line will be at full health going into a big-time AFC North battle. Cleveland’s defense is the heart of the team The defense has been the backbone of this Browns team. Cleveland is allowing 20.9 points per game, which ranks 12th in the NFL, and the defensive line has been a clear strength. Even without Myles Garrett, the Browns are getting after the quarterback at a high level. Cleveland ranks third in the NFL with 20 sacks. The Green Bay Packers lead the league with 22 sacks, and they’ve played one more game than the Browns. Having Hall back will help that pass rush. Pittsburgh will see a full rotation up front, and the Browns can keep fresh bodies on the field late in the game. That matters against a division rival on the road. Browns injury report question marks for Sunday Overall, the Browns are about as healthy as they could ask to be at this point in the season. Cleveland already beat Pittsburgh once, and now it has a chance to do something the franchise hasn’t done in decades. The opportunity is right there for the Browns on Sunday, and they have the chance to finish the job in Pittsburgh. This article was originally published on A to Z S

away.headline: Browns get huge injury news before Week 8 game vs. Steelers
away.blurb: According to KPRC 2's Aaron Wilson, Browns starting right tackle Tytus Howard , who was questionable to play in Week 8, has cleared concussion protocol and isn't carrying an injury designation into Sunday's game. Howard, who was drafted by the Houston Texans in the first round of the 2019 NFL Draft, spent his first seven seasons in Houston before being traded to the Browns in March 2026. He suffered a concussion during Cleveland's Week 7 matchup against the Tennessee Titans and did not return to the game. Howard missed all three practices ahead of Week 8 but is now cleared to play against the Steelers . While Howard is good to go for Week 8, the same can't be said for two other Browns players, who remain questionable for Sunday's matchup against the Steelers. Pittsburgh previously ruled out two players and deemed another questionable to play in Week 8, with the inactive report giving us a better idea of his availability. The Pittsburgh Steelers ' Week 8 opponents, the Cleveland Browns , received a huge injury boost ahead of their divisional clash this Sunday. It's their last division matchup before closing the year with three straight NFC South games. Will McFadden Senior Reporter FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — The Atlanta Falcons will take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers for the 66th time on Sunday, reigniting a series that has been exceptionally close. Atlanta leads the head-to-head 33-32, and each of the last six games between the two teams has been decided by six points or fewer. That includes the Falcons' 29-28 victory last season in Week 15, which featured a 15-point, fourth-quarter rally by Atlanta and a career game from tight end Kyle Pitts. Both teams head into this game off rejuvenating wins. A potent rushing attack that generated 258 yards on the ground and a defense that created four turnovers propelled the Buccaneers to a 43-13 win against the Carolina Panthers. The Falcons also forced four turnovers and got a strong performance from quarterback Michael Penix Jr. to earn a 29-20 win and hand the San Francisco 49ers their first loss of the season. After the Panthers lost to the Green Bay Packers Thursday night, the Falcons would gain sole possession of first place in the NFC South with a victory on Sunday. Here's a look at who the experts predict will win on Sunday between the Falcons and Buccaneers. picks.blurb: Falcons vs. Buccaneers Expert Pick | NFL Week 8 2026 Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE KREWE MEMBERS The national analysts are leaning towards the Falcons in Sunday's NFC South showdown at Raymond James Stadium, but some expect a motivated Baker Mayfield to swing the balance Scott Smith Senior Writer/Editor The Tampa Bay Buccaneers come back home in Week Eight trying to turn a rousing road victory at Carolina into a streak within NFC South divisional play, as the Atlanta Falcons visit on Sunday. The Falcons are also riding high, having dispatched a previously unbeaten San Francisco 49ers team last Sunday, and they bring serious firepower to Raymond James Stadium in the quartet of Michael Penix, Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts. To find out how to watch, listen and livestream the game, click here . Several analysts noted that both teams want to run the ball but will be facing defenses that are hard to run against. One analyst called the two squads "mirror images" in their strengths and weaknesses. One reporter suggested this was a Baker Mayfield game – that his performance would swing the balance – and that he might have some extra motivation going against a Kevin Stefanski-led team. Another pointed out that both teams have struggled to make winning plays at the very end of one-score games, and yet another thought the possible return of Emeka Egbuka for the Bucs would be significant. Perhaps the expert who put it best was the one who called it a "box of chocolates" game with these two teams: You never know what you're going to get. Bleacher Report's Ian Hanford sided with the Falcons in a tight matchup and explains why: "Both the Falcons and Buccaneers have stellar run defenses, so this game may come down to which QB plays better. The Bucs beat the Panthers in Baker Mayfield's return to the field, but that was more about leaning on the run game than Mayfield steering the ship. Michael Penix Jr. has six touchdowns in his last two starts, including three in the Falcons' Week 7 upset win over the 49ers. I think Atlanta will carry that momentum and earn a big NFC South win here." The Buccaneers are 1.5-point favorites at home but the majority of analysts seem to disagree with that assessment. Here's what some of them are predicting will occur on Sunday at Raymond James Stadium: NFL.com – Huzzah to Dan Parr and Brooke Cersosimo, but it's still 3-2 in favor of the bad guys ESPN.com – The Elite Eleven experts still dismiss the Bucs, but this time at least it is 6-5 CBSSports.com – Pete Prisco foretells a six-point win for the Buccaneers USA Today – This group of six is decidedly down on the Bucs, going 5-1 in the Falcons favor Bleacher Report – Ouch. away.headline: Buccaneers get a major boost from latest injury report ahead of Week 8 vs. Falcons
away.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. Emeka Egbuka, who missed last week due to a concussion and foot injury, was a limited participant and has a chance to play against the Falcons. But Irving and Godwin were each given rest days, so Goedeke is the only player truly out with an injury as things currently stand. All in all, it’s hard not to be encouraged with Winfield making his return and Egbuka having a chance to do the same. Both teams will be overwhelmingly healthy entering Week 8, so there are no excuses. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 will make or break the season, and the Bucs need all hands on deck to keep their playoff hopes alive. Buccaneers get encouraging injury news at the perfect time ahead of Falcons showdown Josiah Trotter, who missed practice earlier in the week due to an illness, returned as a full particplant on Thursday. Kenny Gainwell, coming off his best game as a Buccaneer with 88 rushing yards, returned to practice after missing Wednesday with a hip injury. Tampa Bay is getting healthy at the perfect time. Luke Goedeke could be Buccaneers' only key absence in Week 8 The only three players who didn’t practice were Luke Goedeke, Bucky Irving and Chris Godwin Jr. While being without their premier starting right tackle is far from ideal, the Bucs’ offense operated just fine with Benjamin Chukwuma as the starting right tackle last week. In fact, it was their best performance of the year, allowing zero sacks and rushing for 258 total yards. Todd Bowles went on the record saying that Chukwuma has a “huge future” as an NFL starter , so the coaching staff has the utmost confidence in him as the next-man up. It’ll come down to who executes better and the Buccaneers have a golden opportunity to make a statement in a game that could have massive implications for the NFC South race. 4 key matchups to watch as Buccaneers face the Falcons in Week 8 5 Buccaneers who need to thrive in Week 8 vs. Falcons Panthers’ loss to Packers just gave the Buccaneers a golden opportunity in NFC South Todd Bowles had the perfect message for the Buccaneers after blowout win over Panthers Buccaneers down several key players as latest injury report paints ugly picture This article was originally published on thepewterplank.com as Buccaneers get a major boost from latest injury report ahead of We

home.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. Emeka Egbuka, who missed last week due to a concussion and foot injury, was a limited participant and has a chance to play against the Falcons. But Irving and Godwin were each given rest days, so Goedeke is the only player truly out with an injury as things currently stand. All in all, it’s hard not to be encouraged with Winfield making his return and Egbuka having a chance to do the same. Both teams will be overwhelmingly healthy entering Week 8, so there are no excuses. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 will make or break the season, and the Bucs need all hands on deck to keep their playoff hopes alive. home.headline: Buccaneers Week 7 snap counts: Diaby shines in limited snaps
home.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
home.blurb: This article originally appeared on Bucs Wire: Buccaneers Week 7 snap counts: Diaby shines in limited snaps The Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' Week 7 snap counts show how much production they got from their defensive rotation in Sunday's 43-13 win over the Carolina Panthers , especially from edge rusher Yaya Diaby. According to the official NFL gamebook , Tampa Bay played 63 offensive snaps and 56 defensive snaps. Diaby recorded three sacks for 21 lost yards while playing just 22 defensive snaps (39%). It was his first career three-sack game, and he accounted for three of Tampa Bay's five sacks despite playing fewer than half the defensive snaps. Rookie edge rusher Rueben Bain Jr. led the position group with 37 snaps (66%), followed by David Walker with 30 (54%). Keionte Scott played 34 snaps (61%), while Vita Vea and Calijah Kancey each logged 29 (52%). In the secondary, Jacob Parrish and Zyon McCollum played all 56 defensive snaps, with Ifeatu Melifonwu playing 55 (98%) in Antoine Winfield Jr.'s absence. Offensively, rookie tackle Ben Chukwuma played all 63 snaps for the injured Luke Goedeke. Center Graham Barton also played every snap, while Tristan Wirfs, Ben Bredeson and Cody Mauch each logged 57 (90%). The six-snap difference reflected late-game substitutions after Tampa Bay had built a commanding lead. The running back rotation featured Bucky Irving on 37 snaps (59%), Kenneth Gainwell on 19 (30%) and Sean Tucker on nine (14%). The trio combined for 246 rushing yards and three touchdowns on 45 carries. Tampa Bay finished with 258 rushing yards on 49 attempts, averaging 5.3 yards per carry. Tight end usage offered another look at Tampa Bay's offensive approach because of injuries to their wideouts. Cade Otton played 56 snaps (89%) without recording a reception, while Payne Durham logged 29 (46%), Bauer Sharp played 16 (25%), and Ko Kieft appeared on six (10%). With the Buccaneers attempting just 11 passes, the position group's involvement went well beyond receiving. Chris Godwin led Tampa Bay's receivers with 46 snaps (73%), followed by Tez Johnson with 41 (65%) and Ted Hurst with 35 (56%). Johnson caught two passes for 33 yards and a touchdown, accounting for more than half of the team's 64 passing yards. The snap counts illustrate two distinct parts of Tampa Bay's performance. The offense leaned heavily on its running backs and tight ends, while the defense generated pressure through a rotation that kept its edge rushers' workloads relatively low, and Diaby's three-sack outing best exemplified that production.

picks.headline: 4 Bold Predictions in the Jaguars' Showdown With the Colts, Starting With Josh Hines-Allen
picks.blurb: Josh Hines-Allen and the Jacksonville Jaguars have heard about the pass rush all bye week. Jacksonville is paying Hines-Allen, Travon Walker and Arik Armstead a combined $63 million this season, and the three have 4.5 sacks through six games. The Indianapolis Colts come to EverBank Stadium on Sunday with a quarterback who goes down a lot. Indianapolis (2-5) has lost three straight, fired general manager Chris Ballard and then traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner on Tuesday. Jacksonville (4-2) comes off a 34-31 loss to Houston in London and has won the last two meetings in the series. “This has to all be about our improvements, us getting back on track,” head coach Liam Coen said Wednesday, per the team’s website . The Jaguars are a big home favorite . Here are four bold predictions for the first game out of the bye. Josh Hines-Allen leads a four-sack day Daniel Jones has been sacked 19 times, per NFL.com , including six times against Tennessee and four more in Minnesota. Now he’s without Nelson, and rookie fourth-round pick Jalen Farmer is expected to take over at left guard . Hines-Allen has 17 pressures and a 77.1 grade that ranks 18th among 113 edge defenders, according to PFF . Walker leads the team with two sacks. We laid out the pass-rush fix the Jaguars need during the bye, and this is the matchup to make it. Bold prediction: Jacksonville sacks Jones four times, and Hines-Allen gets at least one. Parker Washington goes over 100 yards Parker Washington has 26 catches for 416 yards and four touchdowns, and his 81.6 grade ranks 13th among 76 receivers, according to PFF . He went for 124 yards and two scores against Philadelphia in London, and he has become Trevor Lawrence’s top target . Indianapolis is thin at corner. Sauce Gardner has a 62.6 coverage grade, 47th among corners, per PFF , and was limited Wednesday with a calf injury before practicing fully Thursday. Justin Walley missed both days with a knee injury, and the Colts put Cam Taylor-Britt on injured reserve this week. Bold prediction: Washington tops 100 yards and catches his fifth touchdown. Travis Hunter intercepts Daniel Jones Travis Hunter caught a touchdown and picked off C.J. Stroud in the end zone in London, per the Jaguars . He has two interceptions on 311 snaps at corner, and his 69.0 coverage grade ranks 23rd among 101 corners, according to PFF . Jones has seven interceptions, and his 48.3 passing grade ranks 32nd of 35 quarterbacks, according to PFF . Jacksonville’s pass defense still has communication issues to clean up , and defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile put it simply. “No defense can overcome giving up chunk plays,” he said, per the team’s website . Bold prediction: Hunter gets his third interception. Brian Thomas Jr. catches a touchdown Brian Thomas Jr. has nine catches for 105 yards, and he was benched at halftime in London after a career-low 15 snaps. “I really just wanted to flush it, come back ready with a different mindset, come back ready to go,” he said this week, per The Associated Press . His name sits at the top of the Jaguars’ trade rumors ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline, but Coen expects him to help. “He’s going to be able to help us make plays this week. I bet it. I know it,” Coen said, per The Associated Press . Bold prediction: Thomas catches his second touchdown of the season, and Duval gets a reminder of why the Jaguars drafted him in the first round. away.headline: Colts' injury report includes good news on Tyler Warren, Sauce Gardner, bad news on Justin Walley
away.blurb: Indianapolis will be without starting slot corner Justin Walley , who suffered a knee injury late in Sunday’s road loss to the Vikings and did not practice this week, as well as the team’s first corner off the bench, veteran Cam Taylor-Britt , who landed on injured reserve this week with a groin injury also suffered late in Sunday’s 16-10 loss. The Colts will also get back starting tight end Tyler Warren , who missed the team’s last two games with a groin injury. Warren logged his first practice of any kind Thursday after suffering the injury Oct. 23 before a Week 6 game against the Titans where he didn’t appear as a game-time decision. Warren, the team’s leader in catches (30), missed all of last week’s practice, too, as well as the Week 7 game. He was limited in Thursday’s practice but then participated fully Friday. Along with Walley, the Colts also ruled out wide receiver Anthony Gould for Sunday’s game as the return specialist continues to work his way back from a concussion suffered in Week 6. Gould returned to practice this week and was full both days but needs to clear the league’s concussion protocol. Tight end Drew Ogletree (knee) and Bryce Boettcher (groin) are listed as questionable for Sunday’s game. Ogletree was limited in Thursday’s practice and then did not participate Friday, and Boettcher missed both outings after practicing once last week but missing Sunday’s Week 7 game. With Boettcher’s role Sunday in question, all signs point to rookie linebacker C.J. Allen making his first start of his NFL career, as he returns from an ankle injury he suffered last week in practice that sidelined him Sunday. Allen was a full participant in both the Colts’ practices this week. INDIANAPOLIS – The Colts have gotten mixed injury updates at cornerback this week heading into a road divisional game Sunday in Jacksonville as heavy underdogs. Down two of its top four corners, though, the Colts will get starting outside corner Sauce Gardner back after the All-Pro left midway through the team’s Week 6 game with an injury to his left calf. Gardner then didn’t practice all last week and missed Sunday’s game. He was a full participant in the Colts’ two practices this week. Start the day smarter. Johnson (ankle) did not practice on Friday after initially suffering his ankle injury in the second quarter of the team's Week 6 London matchup versus the Houston Texans. His absence clearly puts more pressure on a safety room that has already dealt with attrition earlier this season with Eric Murray, who dealt with a Week 4 concussion that kept him out of Week 5. Notably, there has been no update on the 21-Day windows being opened for offensive lineman Patrick Mekari (back), rotational edge BJ Green (elbow), or rookie defensive end Zach Durfee (upper body). Each player has been on the injured reserve for at least four weeks, with the potential to return as the team comes off the Week 7 bye week. The Colts, on Friday, ruled out wide receiver and starting punt returner Anthony Gould (concussion). Gould is out even though he practiced fully on Thursday and Friday. The fourth-year safety signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2023 and appeared in 42 games with the Buccaneers in three seasons. Merriweather also spent time with the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions during parts of his career, and he signed to the Jaguars practice squad early in September. He was eventually moved up to the active roster, and he now looks like he will have to play a significant role in some facet against the Colts at home on Sunday. "And then when you went and watched him transition to Houston and then watched him throughout the preseason and the regular season on special teams, you could tell he took on some of the identity and ways in which Houston plays," Coen said. "That physicality, running to the football, burning it down and going and playing your ass off. That was something that was intriguing for us as well. picks.headline: Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8
picks.blurb: Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Practice 3 TRENDING College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates Colts open to trading JT Steph breaks Luka's ankles Belichick-Hudson breakup Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:26 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFL teams based in Los Angeles are not having a great first half of the 2026 NFL season. Both the Chargers and Rams combined have three wins on the season headed into Week 8. The Rams are doing all of the heavy lifting here, but even they are having a disappointing season compared to their offseason expectations. It seems a Rams vs. Chargers Super Bowl is not in the cards this season. While both teams have been frustrating, they are in completely different situations ahead of Week 8. The Rams are very much alive in the NFC playoff race, but they need to continue stacking wins to remain competitive. Meanwhile, the Chargers are 0-6 and somehow still think they'll compete by the end of the season. This game means a lot for both teams, but the Rams arguably have much more to lose. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So which team will come out on top in this one? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this Battle for Los Angeles in Week 8 between the Chargers and Rams. Rams, Chargers combine for more rushing yards than passing yards Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Both LA teams built their teams to have a strong running game. Jim Harbaugh is known for his love of pounding the rock. The Chargers drafted Omarion Hampton and built a massive offensive line for that very reason. As for the Rams, Sean McVay has always leaned heavily on the running game dating back to the Todd Gurley years. That has continued into 2026, as the Rams popularized 13 personnel usage and have taken to a new level this season. But just how committed are they to running the ball? When both teams combine their final stats, this game will feature more rushing yards than passing yards. That sounds like a crazy prediction on the surface. So exactly how bold is this prediction? The Rams average roughly 70 more passing yards than rushing yards per game this season, compared to an 82-yard gap for the Chargers. So it would be quite shocking if both teams overcame this 152-yard difference. If this happens, it may require both defenses to ball out against the pass and allow a handful of explosive runs. This is definitely bold, but crazier things have happened. The Chargers dominate the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball If the Chargers are going to have a chance to win this game, they'll have to do so in the trenches. The injury situation for both teams makes this look like a strong possibility. Joe Alt is expected to return from injury for this game. One offensive lineman won't magically turn LA's o-line into an elite unit. However, it could do wonders as he still projects as an elite talent at the position. If the Chargers can count on one side of the line protected, they can always pull out some tricks to protect the other side. It is also important to note that the Rams have only managed 10 sacks in seven games played this season. That puts them at 27th in the NFL and only ahead of pitiful defensive teams like the Dolphins, Eagles, and Cowboys. It really shows that Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, and Poona Ford are injured. Flipping to the other side, the Chargers and Rams look pretty evenly matched in the trenches. The Rams may hold a slight lead, but nothing too crazy. Ultimately, the Chargers' formula for winning this game is predicated on winning the trenches. This is certainly an area where they could gain an advantage. The Chargers will keep Justin Herbert completely clean, not allowing a single sack. Meanwhile, they will sack Matthew Stafford at least twice. That may not be a huge advantage, but it gives the Chargers a fighting chance. Chargers take Rams to overtime, but lose by a field goal Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images It is really tempting to predict that the Chargers will get their first win of the season in this spot. But it just seems too far-fetched. Realistically, the Rams and Chargers are in two completely different worlds on offense. The Rams average more total yards per game than any other team, while the Chargers are statistically a bottom five offense. There's no reason to suggest that will change in Week 8. Furthermore, the Rams absolutely must win this game to stay alive in the NFC playoff race. McVay may be willing to pull out all the stops if this game becomes close, and the Chargers would need to be lucky to survive in that situation. But playing for pride is important too, so the Chargers won't go down without a fight. They just don't have the horses to get the job done. Brandon McManus kicks a game-winning field goal in overtime, cementing himself as the Rams' kicker for the rest of the season. picks.headline: Rams-Chargers preview: 5 questions for Sunday's matchup
picks.blurb: Rams-Chargers preview: 5 questions for Sunday's matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Practice 3 TRENDING College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates Colts open to trading JT Steph breaks Luka's ankles Belichick-Hudson breakup Rams-Chargers preview: 5 questions for Sunday's matchup Cameron DaSilva, Rams Wire Sat, October 31, 2026 at 1:30 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Rams are taking on the Los Angeles Chargers this Sunday in their first meeting since the 2022 season. The Rams are 3-4 and looking to get back to .500, while the Chargers are still searching for their first win. To preview this game, we caught up with Chargers Wire's Gavino Borquez and asked him five questions about the team, including a final score prediction. What on earth has happened to Justin Herbert and this offense? What's gone so wrong with Mike McDaniel as the OC? Chargers Wire: The Chargers sit at 0-6 and rank dead last in the NFL in points per game (15.0) and EPA per play (-0.190). Herbert is playing the worst football of his seven seasons in the league. He has thrown 5 touchdowns and thrown 8 interceptions, tying for the league high, and has taken 21 sacks. The issues are layered. The offensive line and wide receiver group have been ravaged by injuries. Pre-snap penalties have hindered the unit. And the marriage between Herbert and McDaniel's scheme has not clicked. The two spent roughly four hours in film sessions during the bye week working on mutual accountability and finding spots to build on. We will see if it comes together on Sunday. Are there any key players the Chargers are getting back from injury this week coming off the bye? Chargers Wire: Right tackle Joe Alt is officially cleared and returning to the lineup after missing time with a neck injury. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey has been a full participant in practice coming out of the bye, though still navigating final clearance from a concussion, and is expected to play. Who's an underrated player on defense that the Rams should know about? Chargers Wire: While the average casual fan might not know his name, defensive tackle Teair Tart is widely respected by offensive linemen as a player they need to account for. Tart is known for his run defense prowess, but he has flashed effectively in generating interior pressure. Do the Chargers have any playmakers who can threaten the Rams defense besides Ladd McConkey? Chargers Wire: The Chargers don't possess an alpha weapon, but second-year Tre' Harris has flashed potential as a reliable deep threat . In 5 games, he has caught 15 passes on 26 targets for 225 yards, averaging an efficient 15.0 yards per reception. Though his momentum was temporarily paused by an injury suffered in Week 5 that forced him to miss the Week 6 game against the Chiefs, Harris is trending towards on Sunday. Who wins on Sunday and what's the final score? Chargers Wire: While the Chargers benefit from the return of key offensive pieces in Joe Alt and Ladd McConkey, their vulnerability lies right up the middle. The Bolts' struggling interior offensive line is poised to be the Achilles' heel in this game, allowing the Rams' defensive front to consistently collapse the pocket and get to Justin Herbert. Furthermore, even with the Chargers coming off a bye week, it's hard to tell whether they've made any meaningful offensive changes. Expect the Rams to exploit the center of the line and for their balanced offense to score three touchdowns to secure the victory. Rams 24, Chargers 16. Fresh off the bye, the Chargers will now face off against the crosstown rival Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium. The Rams have found their fair share of struggles this season, but they are coming off of a Week 7 win against the Las Vegas Raiders, improving their record to 3-4. The Bolts entered this week as 7.5-point underdogs, per FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under is currently set at 43.5 points. The Chargers struggled mightily against the Chiefs. picks.headline: 4 Bold Predictions as the Rams Square Off With the Winless Chargers, Starting With Byron Young
picks.blurb: 4 Bold Predictions as the Rams Square Off With the Winless Chargers, Starting With Byron Young - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Practice 3 TRENDING College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates Colts open to trading JT Steph breaks Luka's ankles Belichick-Hudson breakup Kevin Parrish Jr. Fri, October 30, 2026 at 7:15 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Byron Young has been the one constant in a Los Angeles Rams pass rush that has lost Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner and Poona Ford to injuries. He has 32 pressures, seventh among edge defenders, according to PFF . On Sunday at SoFi Stadium, he gets a Chargers offense that can't keep Justin Herbert upright. Los Angeles (3-4) won 35-21 in Las Vegas last week, and Matthew Stafford passed Roman Gabriel for the franchise record in touchdown passes. The Rams still sit third in the NFC West . The Chargers are 0-6 and coming off a bye, but Rams head coach Sean McVay isn't buying the record. "I really couldn't care less what the record says," McVay said Wednesday, per the team's website . The Rams are a 6.5-point favorite in the battle for Inglewood. Here are four bold predictions. Byron Young sacks Justin Herbert twice Oct 4, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) is sacked by Los Angeles Rams linebacker Byron Young (0) and Los defensive end Kobie Turner (91) during the fourth quarter at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images The Rams have only 10 sacks, tied for 27th, per NFL.com , and we wrote before Week 7 about how they pressure plenty but don't finish . Young has five sacks by PFF's count. CBS Sports credits him with 4.5. Herbert has been sacked 21 times, tied for the fifth-most in the league, and 21.2% of his pressures have turned into sacks, according to PFF . Guard Kayode Awosika missed practice Wednesday and Thursday with a fibula injury, per the Chargers' injury report . Bold prediction: Young sacks Herbert twice. Blake Corum scores two touchdowns Oct 12, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams running back Blake Corum (24) rushes as Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson (22) defends during the fourth quarter at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Blake Corum ran 17 times for 93 yards and a touchdown in Las Vegas, and he had two more scores, from 2 and 43 yards, wiped out by penalties, per the Rams . Kyren Williams' third-quarter fumble opened the door for Corum , and Williams has lost two fumbles this season. Stafford likes what he has. "I haven't had a tandem like this where they both can do everything," he said on The Pat McAfee Show, per the Rams . Corum has 316 yards on 4.9 yards per carry. Bold prediction: Corum finds the end zone twice, and these ones count. Quentin Lake intercepts Herbert Oct 18, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Arizona Cardinals running back Bam Knight (20) runs the ball against Los Angeles Rams safety Quentin Lake (37) in the first quarter at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Quentin Lake wears the green dot now, and he's earned it. He has two interceptions, and his eight pass breakups lead all safeties, according to PFF . His 79.1 coverage grade ranks seventh at the position. "Having the dot, it's a privilege. It shows that the coaching staff they trust in you," Lake said, per the team's website . Herbert has thrown eight interceptions with 14 turnover-worthy plays, and his 44.5 PFF grade ranks last among 35 quarterbacks. Bold prediction: Lake picks off Herbert for his third interception. Puka Nacua tops 100 yards Oct 18, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (12) avoids the tackle of Arizona Cardinals cornerback Max Melton (16) in the fourth quarter at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Davante Adams is out after cleanout surgery, with a 6-to-10-week timeline that McVay said is projected to land "on the shorter end," per the Rams . That leaves more for Puka Nacua, who has 45 catches for 485 yards. His 90.0 grade ranks sixth among receivers, and he hasn't dropped a pass, according to PFF . The Chargers' secondary is banged up. Safety Derwin James missed both practices with a hamstring injury, and Jim Harbaugh said he could go on injured reserve, per the Chargers . Cornerback Donte Jackson was limited both days. We've asked whether Nacua's body can hold up under this kind of workload, but Sunday sets up well for him. Bold prediction: Nacua goes over 100 yards for the first time since Adams went down. home.blurb: According to a report from longtime NFL insider Ian Rapoport, Micah Parsons is targeting a return to the field for the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve against the Rams. Matthew Stafford and the Rams' offensive line will be going up against one of the best pure pass rushers in recent NFL history. Assuming he does return, the offensive game plan will need to change drastically from what it would have been had Parsons not played. On the Los Angeles side of things, the Rams are certainly hoping that their own superstar pass rusher will be back on the field. Myles Garrett has missed all games since Week 1 due to a knee issue of his own. He has been expected to return to the practice field at some point in the near future. All of that being said, the game against Green Bay is still weeks away. The Rams will need to take care of business this week against the Chargers before taking on both the Washington Commanders and Arizona Cardinals. After that, the return of Parsons will be on deck. Parsons has missed a lot of time for the Packers since suffering a torn ACL and a fully torn meniscus last season against the Denver Broncos late in the year. Green Bay has focused on bringing him along slowly, while focusing on getting him back to fully 100 percent before returning to the field. Needless to say, the likelihood of going up against Parsons will change a lot for Los Angeles in that game against the Packers. In his first season with Green Bay last year following the shocking blockbuster trade between the Packers and Dallas Cowboys, Parsons showed why the team gave up two first-round picks and Kenny Clark. He racked up 41 tackles, 12.5 sacks, two forced fumbles, and a defended pass in 14 games played. It's always good to see NFL stars healthy and on the field. For Los Angeles, it would have been more ideal to be able to avoid Parsons, but that likely won't end up being the case.

home.blurb: Rams Injury Report: Multiple Key Starters Questionable vs. Chargers in Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Rams Injury Report: Multiple Key Starters Questionable vs. Chargers in Week 8 The Los Angeles Rams could be managing several injuries in Week 8 as they take on the Los Angeles Charger s. Center Coleman Shelton, tight end Colby Parkinson, wide receiver Jordan Whittington, and cornerback Trent McDuffie were all listed as questionable for Sunday's game while long snapper Joe Cardona was listed as doubtful. Shelton is one of the bigger names on that list given his role as the starting center on the offensive line. Shelton was a non-participant in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but was upgraded to a limited participant on Friday. Another player the Rams will be closely watching heading into Sunday's game is McDuffie, who has missed the last two weeks with a groin injury. While McDuffie was a limited participant in practice all week, he will be listed as questionable against the Chargers. McVay was hopeful about McDuffie going into Sunday, but the Rams can feel confident with the players behind him as Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes have each played well. Additionally, Parkinson didn't participate in practice all week. If Parkinson is out, it would likely leave the Rams with just Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen, and Max Klare at tight end and limit what the offense could do out of 13 personnel. Parkinson is extremely valuable in those formations, especially with his ability as a blocker in the run game. Popping up on the injury report on Friday was Whittington. McVay noted that Whittington's back locked up in practice, which is why he'll be listed as questionable. On the Chargers' side, they'll be without guard Kayode Awosika, safety Derwin James Jr., defensive back Deane Leonard, and wide receiver Brenan Thompson. All four players have been ruled out. Additionally, cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley will be questionable with hamstring injuries. However, seven weeks later, the Broncos have been through a gauntlet to open the season, and they've built up a sizable callus through seven weeks of brutal resistance training. Denver has weathered a very tough schedule to open the 2026 season, beating the Los Angeles Rams, Seattle Seahawks, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Chargers and Arizona Cardinals to begin the year at 5-2. While Denver’s offense has not been great (22nd in EPA/Play), the defense is a top-10 unit once again. Nix and Co. seemed to find a rhythm in a win over Arizona in Week 7, and they’ll look to carry that into a home date against Mahomes and the one-loss Chiefs. Kansas City dominated Denver at home in Week 1, winning by three touchdowns, but it’s coming off a shaky performance against the Seattle Seahawks in a loss in Week 7. The Chiefs are still 5-1 this season, but they scored just three points in their last game and failed to reach the red zone on a single possession. Will a Denver defense that has been red hot in recent weeks be able to slow down Kenneth Walker III and this Chiefs attack? All season long, the SI Betting team has been sharing final score predictions as a fun way to help bettors decide on their spread, moneyline and total bets. Plus, we’ve hit a few exact scores, which can make for a fun long shot bet from time to time during the season. With a ton at stake in this matchup – including first place in the AFC West – here’s a look at my prediction for the Chiefs vs. Broncos rematch in Week 8. Chiefs vs. Broncos Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Chiefs -1.5 (-105) Broncos +1.5 (-115) Broncos: -102 40.5 (Over -112/Under -108) There hasn’t been much movement in the odds for this game, as the Chiefs opened as 1.5-point road favorites even with their loss to Seattle on Sunday night. The total has dropped a point from 41.5 to 40.5, and it’s worth noting that the UNDER hit in this matchup in Week 1 with the Chiefs winning 31-10. Chiefs vs. Broncos Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite bet for every single game in his Road to 272 column , and he’s buying the Chiefs on the road in this AFC West showdown: The Broncos' offensive issues and Bo Nix's play are going to haunt them against a good defense sooner rather than later. Their offense is 23rd in EPA per play and 29th in success rate, making them one of the worst offenses in the league through the first seven weeks. Now they take on a Chiefs team that has been impressive defensively, ranking fifth in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. I'd like to see the Chiefs' offense lean on the run game even more moving forward, as they rank in the top three in every offensive rushing metric. They can use that weapon against a Broncos defense that has struggled to stop the run compared to recent seasons. They're 27th in opponent rush EPA. If the Chiefs can lean on their run game and continue to play good defense, they're going to get the road win and cover the short spread. A lot of this game comes down to two things: Do you believe in the Denver offense after a strong Week 7? And, how much stock do you put into Kansas City’s Week 1 win at home? The Broncos are still just 22nd in EPA/Play, 29th in success rate and 26th in yards per play on offense. That isn’t going to cut it against Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker III, especially since Denver is allowing 4.6 yards per carry on defense. These teams are No. 5 (Kansas City) and No. 6 (Denver) in EPA/Play on the defensive side of the ball, and the UNDER has hit in the majority of both of their games. I expect another low-scoring affair with the Chiefs’ offense ultimately being the better unit on Sunday. Before Andy Reid's squad could even blink, the Chiefs are suddenly in danger of surrendering the AFC West lead when they take on the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High tomorrow. These division rivals have already faced off earlier this season, when Kansas City took care of business 31-10 in the regular season opener. However, the Broncos have strung together a three-game winning streak during which they have allowed fewer than 16 points per contest. Many Chiefs fans have grown increasingly concerned about the state of the offense after its horrendous three-point showing on Sunday Night Football . When opposing defenses take away Kenneth Walker, KC has struggled to get anything going and create explosive plays. This will undoubtedly be the most pivotal game of the Chiefs' season to date. Let's dive into what the ESPN Matchup Predictor believes will transpire in this AFC West clash. They desperately need to avoid falling in their second consecutive loss and relinquishing the division lead. Things can only trend upward for this Chiefs offense, which mustered up 213 total yards and one field goal a week ago. Now that the outside noise about Kenneth Walker's return to Seattle can be put to bed, the hope is that he and Patrick Mahomes will get back to what they were doing earlier this year. As for Denver, much has been made about Bo Nix and his inability to move the ball downfield, but the Broncos have been winning in spite of his questionable quarterback play. His defense bailed him out time and time again in an overtime thriller two weeks ago, when the Broncos outplayed the Seahawks and won on a walk-off field goal by Wil Lutz. There's no question that the Chiefs have the better offense of these two teams, but the bigger question is whether they can find their footing early or if Denver's defense will stifle it from the jump. If the Broncos can force the Chiefs into playing their brand of football and turn this into a closely contested, defense-oriented matchup, that's where things could get dicey for KC. picks.headline: Week 8 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Chiefs look to bounce back vs. Broncos
picks.blurb: Week 8 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Chiefs look to bounce back vs. Broncos - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Practice 3 TRENDING College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates Colts open to trading JT Steph breaks Luka's ankles Belichick-Hudson breakup Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, October 29, 2026 at 3:49 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the Denver Broncos, Week 1 had to feel like a bad flashback. The first 12 times that Patrick Mahomes started against the Broncos, the Kansas City Chiefs won every time. Then there was a shift with Sean Payton in charge, and the Broncos won two of three against Mahomes and the Chiefs. The 2026 season opener, though, was like old times. It wasn't Mahomes that ruined the Broncos in the opener, though he played pretty well. It was Kenneth Walker III doing most of the damage, as he ran through many Denver missed tackles for 173 rushing yards. Also, the Chiefs' defense shut down Denver in a 31-10 win. It was a complete, impressive performance. It doesn't seem like much has changed since then. The Chiefs started 5-0 before losing last week at Seattle, a very tough opponent. The Broncos are 5-2 but questions persist about their offense. While the defense on the whole has been better for the Broncos, the run defense isn't great. Denver is 26th in EPA ( expected points added ) per rush allowed. It's easy to say that the Seahawks showed everyone how to beat the Chiefs — take Walker out of the game — but not everyone has Seattle's defense to pull that off. The Broncos showed once they aren't a great matchup against Walker. That's a big reason Kansas City -1.5 is the pick. We saw in the season opener that the Chiefs' dominance over the Broncos might not be over. Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III had 173 rushing yards in Week 1 against the Broncos. (AP Photo/Colin E. Braley) Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 8 of the NFL season: Panthers (+3.5) over Packers There's no way the Panthers are as bad as they played last week, when they were down 33-6 to the Buccaneers by halftime. Competent teams that get embarrassed usually bounce back well. The Packers are still a tough team to predict. Raiders (+1.5) over Jets The early East Coast start has been death for the Raiders for a long time, but they are probably the better team. They are certainly the better coached team. The Raiders are on a four-game losing streak but look at the opponents: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills, Rams. Those are four of the strongest teams in the NFL. If Las Vegas can't win here, it might be Fernando Mendoza time. Cowboys (-6.5) over Cardinals The Cowboys are going to score. The Cardinals have given up at least 30 points in six of their eight games. Dallas showed on Monday night that its offense is back, but what about the defense? Maybe a strong fourth quarter against the Eagles is a sign that the Cowboys' defense can be somewhat competent. It's scary to pick the Dallas laying points to anyone because they'll need to get stops, but it would be a surprise if they don't score 30. Buccaneers (-2.5) over Falcons Good luck figuring out either of these teams. The Buccaneers could be better than we think. Their only significant weakness has been pass offense, and that is explained by having an undrafted rookie starting three of their seven games. We don't know if Baker Mayfield is fully healthy, considering he had just 11 pass attempts in his return from a dislocated right thumb last week, but if he is maybe the Bucs can get on a roll. Browns (+3.5) over Steelers Teams coming back from an international game and playing right away without a bye are 0-3-1 this season. The losses were by 12, 11, and 6 points, and the close loss was by the Texans as a 10-point favorite last week. The tie was the Commanders when they were favored at home against the Giants. It's a hard turnaround, and it's what the Steelers face coming back from Paris last Sunday. Both of these teams are 5-2 but flawed, and I'll ride with the angle of the Browns not being the team that played in France last week. Jaguars (-9.5) over Colts It's hard to imagine being a Colts player this week. Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were traded and everyone else with any value has to wonder if they're next. It's actually surprising the line is less than 10 points against a Jaguars team coming off a bye and a loss. This one could get really ugly. The remainder of the Colts' season could get really ugly. Ravens (+3.5) over Bills You've seen this here before: This all depends on if Lamar Jackson plays. This week, I assume he will. It seemed like he was close last week and he practiced in full on Wednesday. There would be some real frustration if he's not back for this game, which Baltimore might need to win to start to save its season. The Ravens' remaining schedule is the toughest in the NFL, according to DVOA . If he does play, we know the Bills defense is not very good. Getting more than a field goal seems good. Vikings (+3.5) over Lions If the Vikings' build was reversed, and they had a fun offense that was clearly one of the two best in the sport but a defense that was unreliable and among the 10 worst in the NFL, we'd respect them more. How do we know that? The 2026 Buffalo Bills, that's how. Minnesota's defense has been remarkable. Look at the Chicago Bears this season. In three of Caleb Williams' four starts, Chicago is averaging 39 points. In the other start, against the Vikings, the Bears scored three points at home (Williams got injured in that game but not until the middle of the fourth quarter). Maybe Detroit will figure out Brian Flores' defense, but nobody else has and I'm willing to take more than a field goal with the Vikings. Titans (+10.5) over Bengals The Titans have been blown out only twice. They lost by 13 to the Jets in Week 1 and 23 to the Texans in Week 5. Every other game has been decided by six or fewer points. The Titans have won only one of those games, but they're keeping it close. It's possible Joe Burrow will add to his growing MVP argument and torch Tennessee in a blowout, but this seems like a good spot for an ugly underdog. Rams (-6.5) over Chargers Typically, an 0-6 team coming off a bye would be a fine choice. The Chargers don't want to get embarrassed all season, but they're simply not a good team in any phase. That is shocking but also irrefutable. This is the exact type of contrarian pick I'd like to make but I just can't get there with the Chargers. Patriots (-7) over Dolphins It's possible the Dolphins get some confidence from their first win. It's also possible they let down a bit: It's still a 1-5 team whose goal was to get that first win out of the way. On the other side, there's a Patriots team coming off a loss with three extra days of rest. Commanders (-5.5) over Eagles A low point of this week was looking at the schedule and realizing this was the Sunday night game. Not fun. Not sure what's more surprising: That a 1-4-1 Commanders team is a 5.5-point favorite over the Eagles, or that the Commanders are the pick. The Eagles' best remaining effort was going to come on a Monday night against the rival Cowboys, and that effort was pretty meager. It won't get better. Bears (+3) over Seahawks The Sunday night game might not be good, but Monday night makes up for it. This one is fun (and should have been the Week 1 opener, but that's an old gripe). If there's an offensive coach that can figure out the Seahawks' defense, it's Ben Johnson. Caleb Williams has been on a heater since returning from a hamstring injury. Bet on the Chicago Bears to cover the spread on Monday night at sportsbooks On the other side, Seattle's offense will be happy to see the Bears defense after a tough stretch of opposing defenses, and perhaps Jaxon Smith-Njigba goes wild. It should be a good game, and if that holds true it'll be nice to have the underdog. Last week : 5-8-1 Season to date: 46-58-2

(Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ian St. Clair Wed, October 28, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The first game of the 2026 season for your Denver Broncos did not go according to plan. Not that anyone in Broncos Country needs a reminder. Denver was flogged 31-10 by the Kansas City Chiefs. And the Broncos defense still hasn't tackled Kenneth Walker. Thankfully, and hopefully, Denver gets a crack at a redo this Sunday in Denver. A win at home against Patrick Mahomes, Walker, and Kansas City would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West. FanDuel Sportsbook has Denver as the home underdog at +1.5 points, though that's basically a pick 'em at this point. The total sits over/under 40.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -115. Offensive Rankings Kansas City : Sixth in total offense (380.5 yards per game), fifth in rushing offense (141.5 YPG), 11th in passing offense (239.0 YPG), 14th in scoring offense (23.8 points per game). Denver : Thirtieth in total offense (270.0 yards per game), 24th in rushing offense (94.9 YPG), 27th in passing offense (175.1 YPG), tied for 24th in scoring offense (20.6 points per game). Defensive Rankings Kansas City : Fourteenth in total defense (323.3 yards per game), 13th in rushing defense (99.5 YPG), 17th in passing defense (223.8 YPG), second in scoring defense (17.2 points per game). Denver : Twenty-third in total defense (349.0 yards per game), 28th in rushing defense (133.3 YPG), 12th in passing defense (215.7 YPG), seventh in scoring defense (20.1 points per game). Here are the MHR staff's keys to Sunday's game. Win the turnover battle As we saw in the Thursday night win over the Seattle Seahawks, when the Broncos defense creates turnovers and the offense protects the ball, Denver wins. The Broncos have been better at creating takeaways this season, and they need to carry that over on Sunday. Force Mahomes into some rushed throws and/or punch the ball out to give Bo Nix and the offense some added possessions. On top of that, Nix and the offense need to continue to protect the ball. Win the turnover battle on Sunday, and the Broncos put themselves in a great spot to win the game. — Ian St. Clair Stop the Chiefs run game Mahomes is continuing to play based off who he was two years ago and not putting in the effort to stay great. I like our chances if we force him to throw on our excellent secondary. Stop Kenneth Walker and win the game. — Sadaraine Tackle Kenneth Walker III The Broncos were hanging tough in the first half in that Week 1 matchup, but the horrific tackling eventually led to big plays in the run game. The Chiefs ran away from Denver in the second half. We all remember how much we overreacted to that first game, but man, did they miss too many tackles to count, and the overreaction was warranted. Since then, however, the Broncos defense has been pretty damn good and the offense is finally waking up. Keep up that momentum, and they should take care of business this weekend. — Tim Lynch Feed Jonah Coleman No need to get cute. Let Jonah Coleman build off the game he had against the Arizona Cardinals. Commit to the running attack. Get the young guys involved. Coleman and RJ Harvey had great games in Phoenix. Keep that going. The passing attack will open up once teams are forced to respect the run. — Adam Malnati Score more points than KC Using advanced analytics, the keys to this game are simple. When the Broncos score fewer points than their opponent, they are 0-2, and when they score more, they are 5-0. Further proving this point, they are 0-1 vs. the Chiefs this season when scoring fewer points than them. However, they were 2-0 against the Chiefs last season when they scored more points than their division rivals. So, according to these advanced analytics, if they can score more points than the Chiefs in this game, they will be 6-2. — Scotty Payne What are your keys to Sunday's game?

away.headline: Chiefs Week 7 injury report vs. Seahawks: Josh Simmons IR move throws wrinkle into KC offense
away.blurb: The distinction is that Simmons’ absence is not new. His IR placement instead eliminates the possibility of an immediate return, forcing Kansas City to keep building around its replacement personnel. For the offense, that makes this a sustained adjustment rather than a temporary bridge to an imminent return. Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson will continue at left tackle, while Joshua Ezeudu is expected to replace Moore on the right side against Seattle. The concern is the combined exposure at both edges. Helping one tackle with a tight end or running back can be manageable. Providing assistance on both sides can reduce the number of receivers available downfield. Moore missed every practice this week and is out with a concussion. Rice also recorded three consecutive nonparticipation listings before being ruled out with hamstring and knee injuries. Smith is out as well, with reporting identifying his injury as a hamstring issue. His absence further reduces the available offensive options. Travis Kelce offers reassurance. Despite limited participation throughout the week because of an ankle injury, he carries no game designation. That is different from being questionable, although it does not establish that he feels completely unrestricted. Defensively, L’Jarius Sneed is questionable after three limited practices with a knee injury. Chamarri Conner practiced fully throughout the week with a knee issue, while linebacker Cooper McDonald remained limited. Neither received a game designation. The central offensive issue remains protection. Simmons’ IR move does not suddenly dismantle a functioning lineup, but it extends reliance on replacements. With Moore and Rice also unavailable, Kansas City must pair sound blocking adjustments with efficient execution rather than expect Mahomes to solve every problem himself. Josh Simmons ’ move to injured reserve extends the uncertainty at left tackle, while Jaylon Moore’s concussion removes another starting option from the offensive line. Kansas City must also play without Rashee Rice and Brashard Smith, creating a challenge that goes beyond protecting Patrick Mahomes . The Chiefs need reliable blocking and alternative ways to distribute touches. away.headline: Justin Tucker Returning To NFL, Joins Kansas City Chiefs
away.blurb: Justin Tucker Returning To NFL, Joins Kansas City Chiefs - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL TRENDING College football live updates Steph breaks Luka's ankles Justin Tucker Returning To NFL, Joins Kansas City Chiefs Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Former All-Pro kicker Justin Tucker is returning to the NFL at the age of 36. Tucker is considered to be one of the greatest kickers in NFL history, which makes sense considering he's made 89.1% of his field goal attempts. His time with the Ravens ultimately came to an end after he was accused of inappropriate behavior during massage sessions. The Baltimore Banner reported that 16 massage therapists made accusations against Tucker, with two of the massage parlors claiming they banned him because of his behavior. "I did not act inappropriately at any point before, during, or after a professional bodywork treatment session, nor have I ever been told I am unwelcome at any massage therapy provider," Tucker told OutKick . "I absolutely respect the massage therapy profession and more so the individuals who work as massage therapists." Tucker has conducted workouts with the Colts, Jets and Saints over the past two years. It wasn't until this Wednesday, however, that he landed a deal. According to Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star, the Chiefs are signing Tucker to their practice squad. BALTIMORE, MARYLAND – DECEMBER 12: Kicker Justin Tucker #9 of the Baltimore Ravens talks to his wife, Amanda Bass, before playing against the New York Jets at M&T Bank Stadium on December 12, 2019 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images)Patrick Smith/Getty Images Harrison Butker has made plenty of big-time kicks for the Chiefs over the past decade, but he seems to be on the decline. Butker has made 11 of 16 field goal attempts this season. He had two crucial misses on Sunday night against the Seahawks.
