home.headline: Broncos' first injury report for Week 8 paints an early bleak picture
home.blurb: Of note, Patrick Surtain II pracitced in full, so the Broncos should get him back, but all of Allen, Waddle, and Talanoa Hufanga did not practice: The initial report with Waddle was that he aggravated his chest injury, but that there is 'hope' he can play on Sunday. Hufanga has already missed a couple of games due to his ankle injury, and if he does not practice in some capacity on Thursday, his status for Week 8 is in doubt. Allen has a hamstring injury and did not practice, either. The weird thing is that there was not any sort of report that came out with Allen's injury like we saw with Waddle, so that could end up being good news that it's pretty minor. We're definitely not going to make any declarations here since it's early in the week, but the Thursday statuses are going to be huge, as if any of the three "DNP" players from Wednesday are limited or full on Thursday, their chances of playing go way up. Sean Payton hilariously called himself out for awful Jaylen Waddle play call The Denver Broncos have consistently been among the healthiest teams in the NFL since Sean Payton took over back in 2023. That doesn't mean, though, the team has not dealt with injuries. Every NFL team has to deal with injuries in some capacity, and the teams that are usually standing in the end have better depth or better roster health overall. In Week 7, a win over the Arizona Cardinals, the Broncos saw two key players leave the game in wide receiver Jaylen Waddle, and defensive end Zach Allen. And in the team's first injury report of Week 8, we see some key players on the report, and while it is early, their statuses for Week 8 could already be in doubt. Denver Broncos injury report is getting longer as Week 8 approaches However, if any of them again do not practice on Thursday, it would logically be unlikely that they play on Sunday. While the Broncos are more talented than Kansas City and get this game at home, not having even one of these players is going to be brutal. In the same way that 2025's home game against the Chiefs was important, this one is as well. The Broncos would be in first place in the AFC West with a win, but if they lose, the Chiefs would improve to 6-1, and Denver would drop to 5-3 with two losses to the Chiefs already etched into their record. It would severely hurt their chances at repeating as division champions. And as it concerns the pasing game, if the Broncos hope to build on their breakout from Week 7, having Waddle in the lineup would allow that to continue to happen. picks.blurb: Patriots vs. Dolphins bold predictions for AFC East clash in NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Practice 3 TRENDING College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates Colts open to trading JT Steph breaks Luka's ankles Belichick-Hudson breakup Patriots vs. Dolphins bold predictions for AFC East clash in NFL Week 8 Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints Fri, October 30, 2026 at 5:29 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New England Patriots will be a rested and motivated team when they take the field in South Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins . The Patriots lost a hard-fought game against the Chicago Bears last Thursday night, but the defeat was a competitive effort that demonstrated they could play on the road against a team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. The assignment this week doesn't compare. The Dolphins lack the kind of talent on either side of the ball to put up a 60-minute fight against QB Drake Maye and a motivated Patriots team. Miami earned its first victory of the season in their Week 7 game against the New York Jets, but they benefitted greatly from an inefficient and sloppy game from the Jets. Patriots feeling good about their consistent level of play It is unlikely that the Patriots will come at them in a similar manner. New England has played four consecutive solid games, and three of them were victories. When they took down the Buffalo Bills on the road in Week 4, it demonstrated that Mike Vrabel 's team was back on track and was ready to make a run at the AFC East title once again. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) They are 1.5 games behind the first-place Bills, so they have quite a lot of work to do to get there. However, they have more than enough focus and talent to get past the Dolphins on the road. As the Patriots prepare for this game , they are fairly confident that their offense is on the right track. Mike Vrabel would like to see his defense pick up its level of play and start to force more turnovers. If New England can assert itself on the defensive side and take the ball away from its opponents, they are going to put games away much earlier in the second half and avoid the tension that comes with a game that goes down to the wire. That's what should happen in this game. Maye will throw for 275 yards and 2 TDs against Dolphins The Patriots will not look at this game as one they will win by merely showing up. Throughout the years, playing the Dolphins on the road has often been a chore that has regularly been unpleasant for the visitors. Even in the prime years of Tom Brady's leadership, the Patriots have regularly been pushed hard by the Dolphins. The Patriots are 17-40 all-time in games played in Miami. Maye will not take the Dolphins lightly. He should be close to his best because he appears to have overcome the poor start he had in early season games in Seattle and Jacksonville. Maye has risen quite a bit in the ranks of NFL quarterbacks after his early struggles. He has completed 141 of 214 passes for 1,784 yards with 13 TDs and 8 interceptions. Maye's ability to get away from the pass rush is a big part of his game. He has run for 211 yards and 2 TDs, but the most important part of his athleticism is his ability to get away from the pass rush and get the ball to his receivers. It seems very unlikely that the Dolphins secondary is going to stop tight end Hunter Henry along with wideouts Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas. The big question revolves around A.J. Brown. He has been limited by injuries this season and has played just three game and has caught just 9 passes for 101 yards. He may or may not be ready to contribute to the Patriots' effort in this game because his knee appears to have flared up. However, the Patriots are expecting him to become their go-to receiver at one point this season. Malik Willis will throw for 150 yards, but toss two interceptions Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images Vrabel wants to see his defense step up quite a bit in the weeks to come. When the Patriots made their charge last season, Maye and the offense got a big assist from the defense as it stepped up by forcing takeaways. The Pats are going to attempt to do this by putting pressure on QB Malik Willis. The former Packer has tried to keep the Dolphins afloat, but the Dolphins have just one win this season. Willis has completed 87 of 151 passes for 1,057 yards with a 4-4 TD-interception ratio. He has also rushed for 223 yards and 3 TDs. Willis has been sacked 16 times this season, and linebacker Elijah Ponder of the Patriots will be after him. Ponder leads New England with 5.5 sacks and should get at least 1.5 in this game. Willis will be trying to get the ball to Malik Washington. He leads the Dolphins with 26 receptions for 289 yards but he has yet to find the end zone. Bold game prediction: Patriots 33, Dolphins 13 The Patriots have too much talent and they are focused on playing consistent, error-free football from this point forward. While many Patriots teams have had problems on the road against the Dolphins, this team will not. Look for Maye and RB Rhamondre Stevenson to get the Patriots off to a good start, and the defense will keep the Dolphins from mounting a charge. The Patriots will have control of this game prior to the end of the third quarter and New England will gain its fourth win in five games. New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown will miss Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins after being unable to practice this week with a knee injury. The team confirmed the news Saturday after Brown missed practice on Thursday and Friday. Brown suffered an ankle injury in Week 1 that sidelined him for four games. He returned for the Patriots' last two contests but indicated he was playing through something in Week 7. Brown took more than 100 snaps in those games, which were played in a span of just five days. He was targeted 16 times and made six catches for 75 yards across the stretch. "I know, obviously, I'm working on something, but there's no excuses," Brown said. Wolf noted at the time Brown had missed just one regular-season game to a knee issue. Brown also downplayed the issue when asked about his knee health this summer. The Patriots also have wide receivers Chandler Brayboy, Kyle Dixon, Cameron Dorner and Ryan Miller on the practice squad . Brown' absence could put more pressure on the Patriots to improve their rushing attack. Quarterback Drake Maye has gained almost as much ground (211 yards) as top running back Rhamondre Stevenson (285 yards) through seven games.

It's been a largely disappointing first half of the season for wide receiver A.J. Brown in his debut campaign with the New England Patriots . Things are possibly about to get worse for the Patriots and their marquee offseason trade acquisition. New England could potentially afford to sit Brown in Week 8 if he's not healthy enough, as the Patriots are heavy road favorites for Sunday's contest versus the Miami Dolphins. New England has a pair of NFC North contenders on deck in Weeks 9 and 10 with the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions, respectively, before its Week 11 bye. The Patriots are just 4-3 this fall, however, so if they want to make a run at their second straight AFC East crown and put pressure on the Buffalo Bills (5-1), they can't take the Dolphins for granted. Brown has played in just three of New England's first seven contests this year as he missed Weeks 2, 3, 4 and 5 due to a high-ankle sprain. The three-time Pro Bowler returned to action in Week 6 against the New York Jets but has yet to have an impact on offense. Brown has played only 132 offensive snaps in his three games and has recorded nine catches for 101 scoreless yards on 20 targets. His longest reception of the season has gone for just 18 yards, but Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said on Monday that he isn't concerned about the 29-year-old's lack of production. Thursday's news still leaves the door open for Brown to take the field and perhaps turn things around on Sunday, but it's not looking great.

away.headline: New Patriots rumors update Christian Barmore's availability at NFL trade deadline
away.blurb: New England Patriots defensive tackle Christian Barmore is reportedly available as the Nov. 10 trade deadline nears, per Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated. "The Patriots are deep in the AFC race, but veteran DT Christian Barmore could be had, having played only 41.9 percent of the team's defensive snaps, falling behind Milton Williams and Cory Durden in the team's rotation." New England selected Barmore with a second round pick (No. 38 overall) in the 2021 NFL draft. He's played 71 games (28 starts) over five-plus seasons. Barmore's best season was 2023, when the former Alabama star amassed 8.5 sacks, 64 tackles (39 solo) and 16 quarterback hits. In April 2024, Barmore signed a four-year, $84 million contract extension, per Over the Cap . Unfortunately, Barmore was diagnosed with blood clots in July 2024, and he ultimately played just four games the following season. He returned to the field in 2025 and became a full-time starter for the first time in his career. Over 17 games (16 starts), Barmore had 29 tackles, 11 quarterback hits and two sacks. Barmore has been productive getting to the quarterback through six games (three sacks). Pats analyst Carlos A. Lopez spoke more on his pass-rushing skills. However, Barmore has seen his playing time dip down from 65 percent of the defensive snaps in 2025, per Pro Football Reference . He has started just one of six games. Head coach Mike Vrabel was asked about that in a recent press conference. We'll see if Barmore sticks around with the Pats after the Nov. 10 trade deadline, but in the meantime, New England is visiting Miami to play the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

home.blurb: Injury Report Analysis: WR A.J. Brown, RB TreVeyon Henderson questionable for Week 8 matchup vs. the Dolphins Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS Brown (ankle/knee) is officially questionable for Sunday's game after sitting out the final two practices this week. On Friday, New England listed WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness), CB Carlton Davis III (neck), and LB Christian Elliss (chest) as questionable for Week 8. On the one hand, the Patriots haven't ruled out any players as their active roster gets healthier. However, several key contributors remain on injured reserve (WR Mack Hollins, WR Romeo Doubs, LG Aijah Vera-Tucker, RG Mike Onwenu), while Brown's participation decreasing as the practice week wore on was a noteworthy development. While still managing his recovery from a high-ankle sprain, Brown's knee reportedly "flared up" in practice this week, which landed him on Wednesday's injury report as limited. Brown then didn't participate in Thursday or Friday's session, but the 29-year-old still has a chance to play on Sunday. The Pats top wideout has caught just 6-of-16 targets for 75 receiving yards in two games since returning from injury. On Friday, head coach Mike Vrabel had an update on Brown's status. As for the offensive line, the Patriots are managing injuries there, too. Starting RT Morgan Moses continues to play through a foot injury while C/G Ben Brown is pushing to get back into the lineup. Brown started three games at right guard before exiting the Patriots Week 6 win over the Jets with a knee injury. Brown was a full participant in practice this week, suggesting he could return to the starting lineup. Moving over to the defense, the positive injury news is that the Patriots secondary is expected to be whole for the first time since Week 3. Although he's officially questionable, CB Carlton Davis III (neck) is trending toward playing on Sunday after participating in full for all three practices this week. Davis has missed three straight games and four of the last six contests due to his neck injury, while top CB Christian Gonzalez has also missed time with a shoulder injury. "Yeah, I mean, it's everything," Gonzalez said of Davis's return. "CD is a great vet. Somebody that I lean on a lot, able to talk to, pick his mind about certain things. He's seen a lot of balls, so just having him back out there is amazing. Excited to get all of us back." Although the wide receiver situation is in flux, the Patriots roster health is trending in the right direction, with OL Ben Brown and CB Carlton Davis III expected to return this week. The next steps for New England are practice squad elevations and downgrades en route to Miami on Saturday. As mentioned, the Pats could elevate a practice-squad receiver due to Brown's uncertain status, with Dixon or Dorner as frontrunners, or practice-squad RB Lan Larison to fill in for Henderson – we'll keep you updated. news Injury Report Analysis: Patriots rule out five play

The Philadelphia Eagles hit the road to play the Washington Commanders, and both of these teams are struggling right now in the NFC East. However, if you don’t want to pick a winner for this game or even the total, you can simply take a player to find the end zone and potentially come away as a winner on Sunday night. There are a bunch of different players to consider in this market, but the Eagles' offense has been banged up all year with DeVonta Smith (out) and Saquon Barkley (set to play despite a hamstring injury) missing time. That has thrust some lesser-known players into big roles, especially with Jalen Hurts out for the season with a blood clot. Backup quarterback Tanner McKee is set to make his third consecutive start, and the Eagles are looking to snap a five-game losing streak that has dropped them into third place in the division. Meanwhile, the Commanders are coming out of their bye week and looking to get back on track after a loss on Monday Night Football in Week 6 to the San Francisco 49ers. Jayden Daniels and company lost Terry McLaurin to a knee injury for the rest of the season in that matchup, which should lead to some new faces carrying the load for Washington at receiver. That opens the door for some interesting decisions in the anytime touchdown scorer market, and I've decided on three players that I like to score with these two rivals facing off. Here's a breakdown of each of those picks and their latest odds for Week 8's Sunday night showdown. Overall, Barkley has suited up for just 32.8 percent of the Eagles’ offensive plays in the five games he’s appeared in, making him a risky bet elsewhere in the prop market. The star back played less than 16 percent of the snaps in Week 7, but he still handled nine touches for 71 yards and a score. The Commanders have only given up five rushing scores in six games, but they may struggle to contain Barkley, even if he’s at less than 100 percent. Stefon Diggs Anytime TD (+215) Stefon Diggs has four touchdown catches in five appearances in the 2026 season for the Commanders, and he’s now the No. 1 receiver with McLaurin done for the year. Diggs has played just 59.8 percent of the Commanders’ snaps on offense, yet he’s been targeted at least six times in every game. That’s led to 24 receptions for 214 yards, and Jayden Daniels has thrown the ball Diggs’ way a ton this season. In fact, Diggs found the end zone and had nine targets against this Philly team in Week 1. I’m buying him to have another big game on Sunday night, especially after he stepped up for six grabs and a score in Week 6. That workload should eventually turn into some scores, and this is a great matchup for the Eagles tight end to make it happen. Philadelphia won that one 24-22 when Washington's tying two-point try was stuffed. Since then, Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for the season with blood clots in his lungs, and the Eagles have lost five straight, their longest skid since 2016. Washington (1-4-1) comes off its bye after a 23-17 loss in San Francisco that also cost it Terry McLaurin, who tore his patellar tendon and is done for the season, according to the team . Head coach Dan Quinn called the week off "a much-needed reset in a lot of ways," per the team's website . Philadelphia (2-5) lost 38-21 to Dallas on Monday night with Tanner McKee at quarterback. The Commanders are about a six-point favorite at Northwest Stadium and hold the EPA edge in nine of 12 categories. Here are four bold predictions for Sunday Night Football. Jayden Daniels leads Washington in rushing Oct 19, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (5) is hit as he throws by San Francisco 49ers defensive end Romello Height (94) during the second quarter at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Daniels has 213 rushing yards on 25 carries, 8.5 per attempt, in four games, and his 88.7 rushing grade ranks third among quarterbacks, according to PFF . He has played the last two games in a brace after dislocating his left elbow in Week 2, and he ran only four times for 10 yards in San Francisco. He was a full participant in practice Wednesday and Thursday. Washington needs him to run. Jacory Croskey-Merritt is on injured reserve with a groin injury , leaving Rachaad White (36 carries, 145 yards) as the lead back. Philadelphia ranks 27th against the run at 131.4 yards per game, and Javonte Williams ran for 155 yards against the Eagles on Monday. Bold prediction: Daniels runs for 75 yards and a touchdown, more than any Washington running back. Washington sacks Tanner McKee four times Oct 4, 2026; Tottenham, ENG; Washington Commanders linebacker Odafe Oweh (98) sacks Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) during the first quarter at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Quinn's defense blitzes more than any team except Minnesota, and it has only 11 sacks, tied for 22nd. "I'd love to see us, whether it's blitzing or rush coverage together, really being in sync with that," Quinn said Wednesday, per the team's website . Odafe Oweh leads the team with three sacks on 15 pressures, according to PFF , though he hasn't played up to his contract yet. K'Lavon Chaisson has 2.5 sacks and two forced fumbles. McKee is working behind a line that has allowed 18 sacks, and the Eagles had no sacks or quarterback hits of their own against Dallas. Bold prediction: Washington sacks McKee four times, even with Javon Kinlaw likely out with a knee injury. Antonio Williams beats Zack Baun this time Oct 19, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; Washington Commanders wide receiver Antonio Williams (14) makes a catch during the fourth quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Week 1 belonged to Zack Baun. Washington targeted him six times in coverage, and its pass catchers finished with minus-2 yards against him, per Next Gen Stats. He added 12 tackles and was named NFC Defensive Player of the Week . picks.headline: Eagles at Commanders predictions for Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season
picks.blurb: Eagles at Commanders predictions for Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Practice 3 TRENDING College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates Colts open to trading JT Steph breaks Luka's ankles Belichick-Hudson breakup Eagles at Commanders predictions for Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season NBC Sports Philadelphia Staff Sat, October 31, 2026 at 7:00 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Eagles at Commanders predictions for Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Eagles (2-5) are on the road to face the Commanders (1-4-1) on Sunday Night Football. Let's get to our predictions: Reuben Frank (5-2) The Commanders aren't very good. They've won one game this year, they're 19th in the league in offense and 25th in defense. Their best running back is averaging 3.8 yards per carry, their best wide receiver is out for the year, their quarterback hasn't thrown a touchdown pass longer than 10 yards. They've already lost to two 2-5 teams, the Colts and Eagles, and they haven't beaten anybody in a month. I'm not sure there's a team I'd pick the Eagles to beat right now. Maybe the Dolphins. It's not really about who they're playing, it's about them. They aren't good at anything. They're the only NFL team ranked 27th or worse on both offense and defense. They don't make big plays on offense, they allow too many big plays on defense, they don't tackle, they don't pressure, they don't stop the run, they don't protect the quarterback, they don't run the ball consistently and they're bad on third down. They're just a bad football team. Do the Eagles have more talent than the Commanders? Sure. I don't think it's close. It doesn't matter. Commanders 24, Eagles 17 Dave Zangaro (6-1) The Eagles are heading to Washington this week to play a one-win Commanders team and are now 5 1/2-point underdogs! That's how bad this season has gotten. The Eagles finally showed some signs of life on offense last week and then the defense totally fell apart. Good teams find ways to win and bad teams find ways to lose; the Eagles are a bad team. Could they go to Washington this weekend and pull out a win? Sure. The Commanders stink too and are without some key players like Terry McLaurin and Jacory Croskey-Merritt. But the Eagles are even more banged up and it can be tough to stop a losing streak like this one. It wouldn't shock me if the Eagles win this game but I'm not picking it. Not after what I have seen the last few weeks. But maybe they can cover. Commanders 26, Eagles 24 Barrett Brooks (4-3) First things first, there is no way the defense plays as badly as they played last week against the Cowboys. Saquon Barkley set the tone early, allowing the offense to run the ball, which set up play action. Tanner McKee settled down in the offense using the quick game. You could see that Makai Lemon was comfortable being the first passing option. The defense felt embarrassed by the poor performance we witnessed on Monday. The trenches were poor all around against the run and the pass. There was too much freelancing in jumping gaps and no gap discipline. Linebackers played slow in their reads and no one was ready to tackle. The Cowboys' offense totally dominated us up front. They ran the ball right through the interior of the D-line. Monday's performance was an anomaly and not the norm of what we can expect from this Vic Fangio defense. Eagles 27, Commanders 21 Mike Mulhern (5-2) We've seen teams spiral downward under Nick Sirianni and he's sometimes powerless to stop it. After five straight losses and countless ways the season has been a disaster, Sunday night is setting up to be the final nail in the coffin of the Eagles 2026 season in front of another national audience. The Commanders are heavily favored, desperate to save their season, and coming off their bye. There is almost no reason to think the Eagles will rebound. But for some strange reason I have a feeling they will. The Eagles defense surely had their desire questioned after getting abused by the Cowboys. I expect them to bow up against a depleted Commanders offense. Washington is down Laremy Tunsil and Terry McLaurin for the season, plus top running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt is on IR. Jayden Daniels has been sacked 9 times in the last two games and a (finally?) healthy and motivated front should be able to get after him. The Eagles offense looked a step beyond competent against Dallas, though that likely had a lot to do with the opponent. Seeing Saquon Barkley back on the practice field on Friday was a big boost. He's going to try to power through his injuries again and this time he'll carry the Eagles to a win. Eagles 24, Commanders 23 Ashlyn Sullivan (5-2) For two weeks in a row, the Eagles' defense is the reason they lost the game. This matchup against the Commanders would typically be bad on bad – the Eagles offense vs Commanders defense. The Eagles' offense showed promising signs last week, the only silver lining for this team. Saquon Barkley has no injury designation and I was encouraged with the way the Eagles tried to run the ball against the Cowboys. The biggest matchup against the Commanders is the Eagles defensive line vs Commanders run game. The Commanders have not been able to run the ball effectively outside of Jayden Daniels' scrambles. I expect the Eagles defensive line to bounce back from their disappointing performance last week. More than anything, I am picking the Eagles to win this game because they can't lose six games in a row… right? Eagles 21, Commanders 17 Ryan Fowler (6-1) A lot of the country won't tune in to what many expect to be a snoozer on Sunday night, but make no mistake about it that this is a massive football game for both sides in primetime. For the Eagles, it would be great to see a full workload for Saquon Barkley. He was electric on Monday night against Dallas in the first half, and I think he gets back to his ways this week against a Washington front that could be missing a few starters (Javon Kinlaw has already been ruled out.) Away from Barkley, there has to be a plan this week to counter Washington's blitz-heavy defense. They send pressure at the second highest clip in football under DC Daronte Jones, and if the Eagles don't have a plan to get the ball out of Tanner McKee's hands, it'll be a long night. This is a defense that gives up a ton of yards and points, but they also take the ball away consistently to give their offense more possessions. Limiting turnovers will be huge. Defensively, last week was an outlier. It has to be an outlier. It was a historically bad night, and I think Vic Fangio's group comes ready to play in primetime. Overall, not that this isn't an important game for the Eagles — it obviously is — but this is a potentially organizational altering game for Washington. Coming off of a bye, at home, in primetime, being frank, I think Washington HC Dan Quinn loses his job if they don't win, and I think they are going to try and pull out all the stops to win in Week 8. Commanders 21, Eagles 17

away.headline: Saquon Barkley Injury Update: Eagles RB’s Week 8 Status Revealed
away.blurb: Saquon Barkley entered Week 7 with a hamstring injury that limited his workload against the Dallas Cowboys, and the running back suffered a back injury on Monday Night Football. Originally entering the league as the second-overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft , the Penn State product hit the ground running, recording 1,307 yards and 11 touchdowns as a rookie for the New York Giants. He remained an elite running back during his five years with the club before joining the Philadelphia Eagles in 2024, where he immediately led the league with 2,005 rushing yards while playing a key role in the team's championship run. After missing a few weeks of action, Saquon Barkley returned to the field in a limited role and finished Week 7's loss with seven carries for 62 yards and a touchdown to go along with two receptions for nine yards. While he only played nine snaps in the game thanks to the hamstring and back injuries, he will return to the field in Week 8. According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Saquon Barkley is "good to go." Needless to say, this is great news for the Phialdelphia Eagles, as the entire offense is battling an absurd amount of injuries. Philadelphia's second- to fourth-string running backs are all injured, quarterback Jalen Hurts is out indefinitely, and wide receiver Devonta Smith will not play. Quite frankly, the Eagles have no choice but to run their offense through Barkley. away.blurb: RB Saquon Barkley against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 action After not practicing on Wednesday and Thursday with hamstring and back injuries, Saquon Barkley practiced in a limited capacity on Friday and is set to be available against the Commanders. The All-Pro running back missed two games with a hamstring injury before returning against the Cowboys on Monday night. However, Barkley was limited in the game after reaggravating his hamstring and injuring his back. "I feel decent. Good week of work, rehab, so I feel good to go back out there and practice," Barkley said after practice on Friday. "Being smart, listening to the trainers, listening to the strength guys and the strength staff, and just doing whatever I can to get back on that football field. That's what my motivation is. The team signed Jaydon Blue to the active roster after placing Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve. Veteran running back Elijah Mitchell was elevated from the practice squad against the Commanders and could be elevated again this week if the Eagles desire three active running backs. Once Pierce exited the game, Mitchell made an impact receiving out of the backfield. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was a full participant at practice while Jalyx Hunt remained limited. With Nolan Smith clearing concussion protocol, the Eagles will have all of their edge rushers available – a rarity this season. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo was limited in practice all week with a neck injury, but will also be available against the Cowboys. home.headline: Commanders' Daron Payne suffers season-ending foot fracture
home.blurb: The Washington Commanders simply cannot catch a break. Over the last two seasons, their roster has suffered significant, season-ending injuries across the board. In their Week 6 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers, the Commanders lost star wide receiver Terry McLaurin for the remainder of the season. Before that, Jayden Daniels re-injured his left elbow, and Athan Kaliakmanis debuted in the NFL when Marcus Mariota went down with a knee injury. Those are just a few of the things this team has been handed in 2026, and now they’re getting smacked in the mouth with another season-ending injury. On Friday, starting defensive tackle Daron Payne went down with a “significant” injury . Today, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Payne is, in fact, lost for the season with a fracture in his foot. Payne, 29, is in his ninth NFL season after Washington made him the No. 13 overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft. He has appeared in 136 career games for Washington, starting 130 and recording 446 tackles, including 67 for loss, 86 quarterback hits, 38 sacks, eight forced fumbles, six fumble recoveries and one interception. He made the Pro Bowl in 2022, which was his best NFL season. Payne finished that year with 64 tackles, 28 TFLs, 20 quarterback hits and 11.5 sacks. He signed a four-year extension that offseason and will be a free agent at the end of this season. The Commanders’ next challenge is on Sunday night when they host the Philadelphia Eagles , who are, incredibly, more banged up than Washington. Payne’s loss makes getting Jer’Zhan Newton back to practice even more important, and they’ll need him back in game shape as soon as possible. Payne will become the eighth player to land on IR for the Commanders this season, and the most frustrating part is that it happened late in Friday's practice. His loss creates a huge hole on the defensive line, so be on the lookout for roster moves soon. home.headline: Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne reportedly suffers Jones fracture in left foot, ending his 2026 season
home.blurb: Payne, who will turn 30 before next season, suffered a "significant" foot injury on Friday, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . Shortly thereafter, the Commanders officially listed Payne as out for Sunday's game versus the Philadelphia Eagles. In addition to Payne, Washington will also be without defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw, who is out for Sunday with a knee injury. Last season, he registered 46 combined tackles, 3 sacks, 1 forced fumble and 5 passes defended. Payne earned Pro Bowl honors in 2022 with 11.5 sacks, 64 tackles and 18 tackles for loss. Washington's 2018 first-round pick (No. 13 overall) out of Alabama, he has started 130 of 136 games during his career. The nine-year veteran underwent more tests on Saturday, confirming the fracture on the outside of his foot . He will go on injured reserve as a result. The typical recovery timeline from such an injury is four months. The fracture occurred during a team drill, not from a contact play, according to ESPN's John Keim . With Washington holding last place in the NFC East at 1-4-1 , Payne could also have been a trade candidate before the Nov. 10 deadline, but the injury negates any possible deal. Additionally, this likely affects Payne's pending free agency. He's being paid $27.6 million for the 2026-27 season, the final year of the four-year, $90 million contract he signed before the 2023 campaign. His $22.5 million average annual salary ranks 15th at his position, which he would surely like to increase. Payne appeared in six games for the Commanders this year, compiling 14 tackles, 1 sack, 2 tackles for loss and 1 forced fumble.

Gilberto Manzano , NFL Staff Writer Iain MacMillan , Senior Editor, Betting Peter Dewey , Associate Managing Editor, Betting All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Gilberto Manzano Week 8 Upset Pick Miami Dolphins (+250) vs. New England Patriots After getting three consecutive upset picks correct, I need to heat check myself. There’s no better way to do that than taking the one-win Dolphins against Drake Maye and the Patriots. Surprisingly, I have plenty of reasons to like this bet. Divisional games are often close, and New England has a long history of struggling in Miami. Also, the Dolphins have plenty of confidence after beating the Jets last week, and this offense is a lot better with rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas, who contributed two catches for 70 yards and two touchdowns in his first game since sustaining an ankle injury in Week 2. I’m playing with house money, and I’m putting it on the Dolphins. Peter Dewey Week 8 Upset Pick Atlanta Falcons (+114) vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers The Falcons may be the most confusing team in the NFL, but I think their best version is the top squad in the NFC South. I’m buying Atlanta as a road underdog against a Tampa Bay team that is 0-4 against the spread at home and potentially overvalued after a Week 7 rout of the Carolina Panthers. Baker Mayfield (thumb) wasn’t asked to do much, but the Bucs beat up a Carolina defense that has allowed the most yards per carry in the NFL. That won’t be the case against Atlanta, which is No. 4 in EPA/Rush and 12th in opponent yards per play in 2026. Tampa Bay has been great defensively as well (third in EPA/Play, seventh in yards per play), but the offensive upside is capped with Mayfield and Emeka Egbuka banged up. Plus, this Falcons offense has been much better with Michael Penix Jr. under center over the last few weeks. The Falcons are 3-2 when Penix starts, and I love this price against a Tampa Bay team with clear flaws and a quarterback at less than 100 percent. Iain MacMillan Week 8 Upset Pick Chicago Bears (+140) vs. Seattle Seahawks I'm ready to believe in the Chicago Bears. Ben Johnson is clearly the real deal as head coach, and Caleb Williams has improved significantly since last season. Last season, he ranked 39th out of 45 starting quarterbacks in completion percentage over expected. This season, he ranks first at +9.0%. The Bears' defense has also been better than people expected this season, ranking fourth in the NFL in opponent success rate. I still have some concerns surrounding the Seattle offense. It did enough to beat the Chiefs last week, but their running game is still weak, and Sam Darnold hasn't been as efficient as he was a year ago. I'll take the Bears as my upset pick of the week. away.headline: Kyle Monangai injury update: Bears RB will miss a fourth straight game
away.blurb: The Chicago Bears will have to face the Seattle Seahawks without their star second-year running back. Head coach Ben Johnson ruled Kyle Monangai out for Week 8 on Saturday, according to Bears reporter Kevin Fishbain . This marks the fourth straight game that Monangai will miss ever since he first popped up on the Bears' injury report with a turf toe injury. Will Kyle Monangai Return in Week 8? Latest Injury Update on Chicago Bears RB When is Kyle Monangai Coming Back? Injury Update, Return Timeline Ahead of Week 8 The last time we saw Monangai, he had pulverized the New York Jets in the Bears' dominant Week 4 victory at Soldier Field. On a day when D'Andre Swift had trouble with ball security, Monangai carried the rock a career-high 30 times for 146 yards and two touchdowns. His 5.4 yards per carry average through four games was near the top of the league at the time, and he appeared to be on the verge of a breakout season. D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson need to step up in a big way Luckily for the Bears, all hope for a strong running performance in Week 8 is not lost with Monangai's absence. Despite some issues this year, Swift remains a solid running back who had an explosive performance in the Bears' season opener . Even fourth-year veteran Roschon Johnson answered the call admirably in Week 6, carrying the ball 13 times for 51 yards, though he did lose a costly fumble. Don't forget about the Bears' dominant offensive line, either, and how critical that is to the success of any team's running game. The right side of Chicago's line, 2025 All-Pro Darnell Wright and Jonah Jackson, are arguably the best tackle-guard tandem in the entire NFL when it comes to run blocking, and it's why Ben Johnson felt comfortable in the offseason openly admitting that they prefer to run to the right side. It's okay if opposing defenses know this tendency in Chicago's run game; it's not like they're going to stop them anyway. It may be for the best that Monangai doesn't play in Week 8. The Bears will likely want to lean on the arm of Caleb Williams in this matchup anyway, and their defense should be ready to go blow-for-blow with the defending champs since their blockbuster trade for superstar Jefferery Simmons . Besides, after Week 8 the Bears get a favorable Week 9 matchup against the hapless Tampa Bay Buccaneers, then they get their bye week. By then, Monangai should be fully healed up and ready for a postseason push. away.headline: Seattle Seahawks RB Jadarian Price Looking Ready for the Chicago Bears
away.blurb: Seattle Seahawks running back Jadarian Price practiced fully on Friday as he attempts to return from the chest injury that placed him on injury reserve. The Seattle Seahawks could see the return of Price and Zach Charbonnet on Monday when they play the Chicago Bears. Charbonnet was limited in practice on Friday, but he practiced fully on Thursday. With both running backs in good standing thus far this week, the Seattle Seahawks can finally showcase their new-look rushing attack without Kenneth Walker III. The Seattle Seahawks drafted Price with the final pick of the first round in the 2026 NFL Draft. While the early returns from Price are limited, the small sample size showed how impactful his presence was to Seahawks starting quarterback Sam Darnold. On early downs, Darnold owns 10-13 completion ratio with 138 yards passing and a touchdown with Price on the field. Not to mention, Price’s rushing efficiency should only increase with Charbonnet also in the fold. The threat of two running backs will keep defenses guessing as to what the Seattle Seahawks are going to do since both are threats in the passing game as well. It seems likely that the Seahawks have their projected running back room healthy in week eight against the Chicago Bears. The Bears rank 19th in rushing EPA allowed, so a heavy running game will be necessary. Seattle Seahawks Running Back Jadarian Price Practices Fully Before Monday’s Bears Game Another issue that plagues Price so far in his rookie season are fumbles. In three games, he dropped the ball onto the ground twice, which was an issue previously for him as well in college at Notre Dame. The Seattle Seahawks have struggled with turnovers in general though, so this is not necessarily an issue that is exclusive to Price. That being said, with the addition of Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts , Price should be entering a situation where he can succeed right away. The Seattle Seahawks want to establish a physical identity at the line of scrimmage. They have that defensively, no doubt. However, offensively, that identity still formulates. The excellence of Jaxson Smith-Njigba cannot be understated, and the Seahawks will continue with him as their focal point as they should. However, the importance of the running game cannot be understated to limit the pass attempts for Darnold. The Seahawks Running Game Finally Comes Into Focus This Season In week seven’s victory over the Kansas City Chiefs , running back Emanuel Wilson ran for 100 yards on 24 carries. The Seahawks ability to run the ball against an above average Chiefs defense should not be ignored, especially when lacking their top two backs. Regardless of the availability of Charbonnet and Price, the Seahawks running game has risen from the grave . The timing of that could not be more prudent for a Seahawks team that started the season 3-3, struggling to run the football efficiently. Like HEAVY's content? Be sure to follow us . Cole Kmet Update: Why Bears $50 Million TE Won't Catch Another Pass in 2026 Kyle Monangai Turf Toe Recovery Timeline Turf toe is a sprain of the ligaments and joint capsule at the base of the big toe, the joint a running back relies on to push off, accelerate and cut. Recovery runs on a sliding scale. A Grade 1 stretch heals in days to two weeks , a Grade 2 partial tear takes two to eight weeks, and a Grade 3 complete tear can sideline a player for six to 12 weeks or more, sometimes requiring surgery. Those ranges are general medical guidance, not a diagnosis of Monangai. Four weeks and three missed games fit the Grade 2 range. That timeline is typical for an injury that required a specialist and a boot, while milder sprains resolve faster and higher-graded ones linger longer. Chicago has kept Monangai off IR, which requires a minimum four-game absence, because the team expected a shorter timeline. Johnson has called him week-to-week and "trending in the right direction," he said, according to Sports Illustrated .
